stories.title: Pakistan Considers 14-Province Administrative Reform Proposal
stories.summary:
Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal stated that a proposal regarding the creation of 14 provinces in Pakistan is under discussion. According to the plan, Punjab would have four provinces, Sindh four, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa three, and Balochistan three. Furthermore, discussions have taken place regarding granting Islamabad separate provincial status. Iqbal revealed that he wrote to Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif in September, suggesting the creation of a committee to review the debate surrounding new provinces, though no progress has been made yet.

Regarding the administration of the capital, Iqbal noted that the prime minister tasked him with formulating an alternative model. After reviewing global capitals, officials proposed a hybrid system combining local government and a provincial assembly. This model envisions a legislative forum for Islamabad consisting of roughly 25 members, including 21 general seats, three reserved for women, and one for minorities. Additionally, union councils could be established as an elected third tier later on, and boundaries might expand to include parts of Rawalpindi division.

Iqbal emphasized that the issue of forming additional provinces must be addressed prior to the Senate elections scheduled for March 2027. He warned that establishing new provinces afterward could lead to disputes regarding proportionate representation in the 96-member upper house for a period of six years. He also dismissed rumors concerning the introduction of a presidential system, noting no serious proposals exist.

Urging politicians to take charge of the debate instead of remaining evasive, Iqbal pointed out the necessity of administrative reforms. He noted that following the eighteenth amendment, provinces failed to devolve functions, resulting in top-heavy provincial structures. The discussion aims to address these structural issues within the country's governance framework.

stories.title: Defence Minister Khawaja Asif Criticizes Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari Over Governance
stories.summary:
Defence Minister Khawaja Asif responded to PPP Chairperson Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari following a critical speech delivered by the PPP leader addressing new provinces, constitutional adjustments, and the treatment of the opposition. Using a social media post on X, Asif utilized the maxim that anyone claiming equity must come with clean hands, questioning whether Bilawal's hands were clean enough to issue threats or lectures. This exchange highlights deepening tensions between coalition partners PML-N and PPP.

The verbal dispute follows Bilawal's remarks criticizing Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's suggestion to hold a referendum on creating new administrative units. Bilawal argued that referendums in history have always served undemocratic acts rather than democratic ones. He also remarked that the governance system did not collapse naturally but was forced to collapse. Asif countered by stating that systems cannot reset without public support, adding that all individuals connected to the system must accept responsibility and involve the public.

Asif also voiced support for considering public opinion alongside parliamentary debate when deciding on new provinces, stating that public participation makes governance a reality. Addressing Bilawal's support for incarcerated former prime minister and PTI founder Imran Khan, Asif maintained that accountability for politicians is not new and that no politician is exempt. He also criticized the PPP's long-term rule in Sindh, claiming the party shares power in government for profit while the PML-N and Pakistan bear losses.

The exchanges underscore ongoing debates regarding governance, public rights, and political collaboration. Asif stressed that the ultimate objective is to improve the lives of ordinary citizens and ensure that ordinary people can live with dignity. He stated that governance is not a monopoly and that public participation remains essential for a democratic society.

stories.title: Sri Lanka Fights Back to Restrict Pakistan on Day Two
stories.summary:
Fast bowler Lahiru Kumara secured three wickets before lunch to trigger a significant Sri Lanka fightback on the second day of the second and deciding Test match in Rawalpindi. Kumara finished the morning session with figures of 4-58, while Asitha Fernando took 2-56. Pakistan reached 221-7 by the break, holding a lead of 123 runs with three wickets remaining in their second innings, after Sri Lanka was previously dismissed for 98 runs in their first innings.

Pakistan resumed play on the second day with a score of 121-3. Azan Awais failed to add to his overnight score of 47 before Kumara had him caught behind during the third over of the morning. Kumara quickly claimed two more scalps in successive overs by trapping Saud Shakeel leg before wicket for 24 and dismissing nightwatchman Saqib Khan, who was caught behind after scoring 37 runs.

Fernando further dented the batting lineup by trapping Salman Agha leg before wicket for 21. These dismissals resulted in Pakistan losing four wickets during the session while extending their overall lead past the 100-run mark. At the break, Ghazi Ghori on eight runs and Amer Jamal on one run remained the not-out batsmen at the crease.

The match represents the decisive second Test of the series taking place in Rawalpindi. Pakistan aims to capitalize on their remaining wickets to build a challenging target, while Sri Lanka's bowling attack continues to apply pressure following their first-innings collapse.

stories.title: Jeff Bezos Says He Helped Choose Robert Pattinson as James Bond
stories.summary:
Amazon founder and chairman Jeff Bezos revealed that he played a heavy role in selecting actor Robert Pattinson to portray the iconic film character James Bond. Bezos made the remarks during Semafor’s Silicon Valley & The World conference, occurring a day after the company officially announced Pattinson as the next agent 007. Bezos explained that Amazon evaluated a larger group of actors and ultimately screen-tested five individuals by having them perform three scenes in full costume on dedicated sets.

Reflecting on the selection process, Bezos described reviewing the screening tests alongside others for a couple of hours. Although initial considerations included a slight bias against Pattinson because of his existing high level of fame—with thoughts leaning toward a less-known actor—the screen tests proved undeniable. Bezos stated that it was obvious Pattinson possessed the qualities needed for the role and declared him as James Bond.

Robert Pattinson, aged 40, started his prominent film career in 2005 with 'Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire' and later appeared in prominent projects such as 'The Twilight Saga', 'The Lost City of Z', and 'Tenet'. The James Bond franchise stands as one of the longest-running and most lucrative series in Hollywood history, featuring more than two dozen released films centering around the British secret agent known for his sophisticated style and vodka martinis.

The upcoming motion picture marks the inaugural Bond adventure produced under Amazon MGM Studios. This follows a 2025 agreement establishing a joint venture that granted Amazon creative control alongside longtime franchise rights holders Michael Wilson and Barbara Broccoli.

stories.title: Pakistan and Turkiye Discuss Expanding Defence and Aerospace Technology Cooperation
stories.summary:
Turkish Air Force Commander General Rafet Dalkıran met with Pakistan Air Force Chief Air Chief Marshal Zaheer Ahmed Baber Sidhu on Wednesday, November 18, at the Air Headquarters in Islamabad. The two leaders discussed strategies to enhance bilateral defence cooperation in unmanned systems, electronic warfare, advanced aerospace technologies, and indigenous research and production.

During the meeting, Air Chief Marshal Sidhu briefed General Dalkıran on the Pakistan Air Force's ongoing transformation into a technologically advanced force focused on capability modernisation. The Pakistan Air Force chief also offered full support for pilot training, professional development, and capacity-building for the Turkish Air Force. General Dalkıran acknowledged the combat proficiency and progressive modernisation trajectory of the Pakistan Air Force under Sidhu's leadership.

Ahead of the air headquarters visit, the Turkish commander also met with Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at the General Headquarters to discuss regional security and mutual defence ties. These diplomatic and military exchanges follow earlier high-level visits, including an official visit by the Pakistan Air Force chief to Turkiye in May.

Pakistan and Turkiye share robust strategic ties and are co-signatories to several multilateral defence pacts. These include the Makkah Defence Pact signed with Saudi Arabia in August, the Badr defence cooperation pact with Qatar and Indonesia in October, and the Regional Four Group alongside Saudi Arabia and Egypt established in March.

This high-level engagement highlights the growing strategic convergence and shared resolve between Pakistan and Turkiye to build an integrated, technology-driven defence partnership. Both commanders stressed the importance of institutionalised professional exchanges, integrated training, and joint military exercises to foster operational synergy.

stories.title: Sri Lankan Bowlers Fight Back to Restrict Pakistan at Lunch on Day Two
stories.summary:
Sri Lanka staged a strong bowling comeback on the second morning of the second Test at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium on Wednesday, claiming four wickets to restrict Pakistan to 221 for seven at lunch. Despite the visiting attack's success, Pakistan maintained a 123-run first-innings lead.

Resuming their innings at 121 for three after dismissing Sri Lanka for just 98 runs on the opening day, Pakistan added 100 runs in 31.4 overs during the morning session. However, disciplined bowling from the visitors prevented the hosts from capitalising fully on their dominant start. Overnight batter Azan Awais failed to add significantly to his score, departing for 47 after being removed by Sri Lankan pacer Lahiru Kumara.

Kumara led the bowling fightback using pace and movement to trouble the middle order, subsequently dismissing Saud Shakeel for 24 and nightwatchman Saqib Khan for 37. Saqib batted for over an hour before being trapped leg-before-wicket by a dipping full toss. Salman Ali Agha provided brief resistance with 21 runs before falling leg-before-wicket to Asitha Fernando late in the session. At the lunch break, wicket-keeper Ghazi Ghori was unbeaten on eight alongside Aamer Jamal on one.

Kumara finished the morning session as the pick of the bowlers with three wickets, while Fernando provided solid support by taking two wickets. Milan Rathnayake also maintained pressure through economical bowling despite going wicketless.

Although Sri Lanka's disciplined morning spell successfully checked Pakistan's momentum, the home side retained a firm grip on the match with their 123-run lead and three remaining wickets in the first innings.

stories.title: Mustafa Kamal Expresses Disappointment Over Bilawal Bhutto's Remarks on Sindh Divisions
stories.summary:
Federal Minister Mustafa Kamal stated on Wednesday that Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari's recent remarks regarding potential bloodshed over the creation of new administrative units in Sindh caused him deep hurt.

Kamal expressed disappointment over Bilawal's warning, pointing out that the regions mentioned by the Pakistan Peoples Party leader are predominantly populated by Urdu-speaking communities. He asserted that Bilawal was explicitly referring to violence involving the Muhajir community through his statements.

To substantiate his concerns regarding unrest in urban areas, Kamal recalled the widespread destruction in Karachi following the assassination of former prime minister Benazir Bhutto in Rawalpindi. He claimed that during that period, businesses belonging to the Muhajir community in Karachi and Hyderabad were deliberately targeted and burned down.

The federal minister argued that there is no need for unnecessary agitation concerning the ongoing debate over administrative restructuring. He emphasised that establishing additional administrative units is a necessary step for effective governance, maintaining that the state must eventually prioritize measures that safeguard Pakistan over individual political preferences.

stories.title: Haaland's Late Penalty Seals Dramatic Norway Comeback Against Denmark in Nations League
stories.summary:
Erling Haaland scored a decisive penalty deep into injury time to cap a dramatic 3-2 comeback victory for Norway against Denmark on Tuesday, securing their spot in the Nations League quarter-finals. The victory concluded a remarkable year for Norwegian football following their recent World Cup qualification.

Denmark dominated early proceedings in Copenhagen, taking a 2-0 lead through goals from Rasmus Hojlund in the 11th minute and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg three minutes later. Norway began their comeback when Haaland scored in the 37th minute following a defensive error by Mads Hermansen, capitalising after Martin Odegaard pressured the goalkeeper. Odegaard later equalized with a strike from the centre of the box in the 83rd minute before Haaland converted a 96th-minute penalty after defender Joachim Andersen was penalized for a handball.

In League A Group Four's other match, reigning champions Portugal defeated Wales 3-2 in Cardiff to finish top of the group with 15 points. Portugal secured the win through a 70th-minute goal by substitute Carlos Forbs, following earlier strikes by Bruno Fernandes and Pedro Neto, despite Neto later receiving a red card for a second bookable offence. Wales, who scored via David Brooks and Sorba Thomas, finished bottom of the group with three points, while Norway and Denmark finished tied with nine points each, with Norway taking second place.

Elsewhere in the Nations League fixtures, Ukraine secured a 1-0 victory over Georgia, Poland and Sweden played to a 1-1 draw, and Ireland earned a 3-0 win against Kosovo. Additionally, Hungary and Northern Ireland tied 1-1, and Israel played out a 1-1 draw with Austria.

stories.title: Chinese President Xi Jinping Calls for International AI Cooperation at APEC
stories.summary:
Chinese President Xi Jinping urged global powers to increase international collaboration on artificial intelligence and free trade during the opening of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting in Shenzhen. Addressing attendees on Wednesday, Xi emphasized the importance of building digital partnerships and steering technological advancements toward a green, low-carbon economic transition across the region.

Xi also advocated for the removal of trade and investment barriers, stating that China aims to foster a predictable and stable environment for worldwide enterprises. He pledged that Beijing will pursue deep-seated reforms by lowering tariffs, expanding market access, and refining management standards in both the manufacturing and services sectors.

The remarks came ahead of an anticipated meeting between Xi and US President Donald Trump. Global trade tensions have heightened as the summit approached, fueled by US tariffs and subsequent Chinese countermeasures, alongside a temporary bilateral trade truce set to expire in January.

The United States recently announced stricter export controls on advanced semiconductors used for AI model training to address national security concerns. These new measures target chip smuggling and grey-market computing rentals, compounding existing technological friction between the world's two largest economies.

stories.title: New Zealand and India Select Four Seamers for Wellington Test
stories.summary:
New Zealand and India have both confirmed they will deploy four pace bowlers for the opening red-ball match of their two-Test series at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. The pitch is widely expected to assist seam bowling, setting up a competitive start to a busy stretch of six matches in seven weeks for the home side under captain Tom Latham.

New Zealand's pace attack will feature Matt Henry, Jacob Duffy, Nathan Smith, and returning fast bowler Kyle Jamieson. This series marks the first red-ball encounter between the two nations since New Zealand achieved a historic 3-0 series sweep in India in 2024, adding significant weight to the upcoming fixtures.

For the visiting side, captain Shubman Gill acknowledged the difficulty of narrowing down his fast-bowling options, though pace standout Jasprit Bumrah is widely expected to lead the attack. This match will mark Bumrah's first Test appearance in nearly a year, following a warm-up fixture against New Zealand A in Christchurch.

Both teams view the series as critical for the World Test Championship standings. New Zealand currently leads the table after four wins in six matches, while India sits in fourth place. Following the Wellington fixture, the teams will play a second Test in Christchurch beginning November 27.

stories.title: Sindh High Court Summons Report on Implementation of Prison Reforms
stories.summary:
The Sindh High Court’s Constitutional Bench has ordered the Inspector General of Jails Sindh to submit a formal report regarding the enforcement of prisoners' rights in provincial correctional facilities. The directive was issued on Wednesday in response to a petition seeking the strict implementation of jail reform legislation.

During the hearing, the petitioner's legal counsel pointed out that although the province enacted a comprehensive jail reform law in 2019, several key provisions remain unenforced nearly seven years later. The lawyer argued that the government is obligated under the statute to establish policy boards, monitoring committees, and professional training centers within prisons.

Additional legal arguments stressed the mandatory establishment of an endowment fund dedicated to supporting prisoners' families, alongside the activation of proper legal assistance mechanisms. The petition highlights a severe overcrowding issue, noting that provincial jails currently house approximately 20,000 inmates despite having an official capacity of only 13,538.

The high court has formally summoned responses from the relevant respondents regarding these alleged violations and scheduled the next hearing and report submission for December 16.

stories.title: Democrat Mary Peltola Wins Alaska Senate Seat, Giving Democrats Majority
stories.summary:
Democratic candidate Mary Peltola secured victory in Alaska's closely watched US Senate race, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. Media projections confirmed the outcome, marking the party's ninth Senate flip of the midterm elections and establishing a 56-44 majority in the upper house of Congress.

Peltola, a 53-year-old former commercial fisher, made history by becoming the first Democrat to win a US Senate seat in Alaska in nearly twenty years and the first Alaska Native ever elected to the chamber. Indigenous residents comprise roughly 15 to 18 percent of the state's population, representing the highest proportion of any US state.

The victory concludes the final uncalled midterm race and grants Democrats their largest Senate majority since 2009. Combined with control of the House of Representatives, the outcome establishes a powerful legislative bloc that could lead to policy standoffs with Republican President Donald Trump. Peltola achieved 50 percent of first-place votes, clearing the threshold needed to avoid further rounds under the state's ranked-choice voting system.

The campaign drew intense national attention and federal scrutiny following allegations that Democrats helped recruit independent candidate Dan J. Sullivan Jr. as a spoiler to siphon votes from the incumbent. While Peltola's campaign denied involvement, the controversy prompted investigations by Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy and the US Justice Department, with Attorney General Todd Blanche characterizing the recruitment effort as potential fraud.

stories.title: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Government Introduces Demerit Point System for Traffic Violations
stories.summary:
The Khyber Pakhtunkhwa government has officially rolled out a demerit points system targeting drivers who break traffic regulations across the province. Formally issued through a notification by the provincial Transport Department under Section 16 of the Motor Vehicles Ordinance of 1965, the mechanism applies specifically to holders of Public Service Vehicles, Heavy Transport Vehicles, and Light Transport Vehicle driving licences.

Under the newly established guidelines, various offences carry penalties ranging between two and 15 demerit points based on the severity of the violation. Causing a fatal accident carries the maximum penalty of 15 points, while causing serious injuries, fleeing an accident scene, or operating a vehicle with a suspended licence incurs 10 points. Minor physical injuries and driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs both carry eight points each. Meanwhile, offences such as reckless driving, property damage, driving without a valid licence, overloading, running red lights, and dangerous overtaking result in six points. Drivers exceeding speed limits by over 40 kilometres per hour or refusing to obey police orders to stop also receive six points, whereas ignoring flashing traffic signals attracts four points.

Motorists who accumulate more than 10 points within a two-year timeframe will be issued an official warning. If a driver surpasses 20 penalty points within the same two-year duration, their driving licence is liable to suspension. The Transport Department will oversee the tracking of these violations by storing the accrued points directly within the driving licence software system.

The implementation of these points relies entirely on formal recommendations put forward by field enforcement teams alongside decisions made by relevant authorized authorities. This comprehensive policy aims to enhance road safety, curb frequent traffic breaches, and hold negligent drivers accountable in the region.

stories.title: Pakistani Man Sentenced to Over 27 Years for Plotting Against US Politicians
stories.summary:
A federal court in Brooklyn has sentenced a 48-year-old Pakistani national to more than 27 years in prison for orchestrating a 2024 assassination plot against Donald Trump and other prominent American politicians on behalf of Iran. US District Judge Eric R. Komitee handed down the 330-month sentence to Asif Merchant, following his conviction by a federal jury in March for attempting to commit an act of terrorism transcending national boundaries alongside murder for hire.

According to federal prosecutors, Merchant travelled to the United States to arrange political assassinations as retaliation for the 2020 American killing of Iranian military commander Qassem Soleimani during Trump's initial presidential term. The targets outlined in the 2024 conspiracy also included Joe Biden, who was president at the time, and Nikki Haley, who competed against Trump during that year's Republican presidential nomination race. During his trial, which commenced in late February, Merchant testified that he engaged with Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps under coercion to safeguard his family residing in Tehran. He claimed that although his Iranian handler named three figures during discussions, he was never explicitly instructed to execute a specific individual.

Law enforcement successfully neutralized the plot prior to any physical attacks taking place. The operation was exposed after an individual whom Merchant approached in April 2024 to assist with the scheme alerted authorities and subsequently operated as a confidential informant. Merchant was apprehended that same year and maintained a not-guilty plea throughout judicial proceedings. Meanwhile, the Iranian government has consistently denied any involvement in targeting or planning attacks against Trump or other United States officials.

stories.title: US Judge Hands Down 27-Year Prison Term for Iran-Linked Assassination Plot
stories.summary:
A federal court in New York has sentenced Asif Merchant to over 27 years in prison. The sentencing follows an alleged scheme directed by Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps to assassinate a United States politician or government officials.

The case came to light after prosecutors detailed the foiled operation, placing Merchant at the center of the security threat. Courtroom sketches and legal proceedings captured his appearance as the judicial process unfolded in New York.

The matter highlights ongoing geopolitical tensions and security concerns regarding foreign-backed plots targeting American leadership. Federal authorities continue to investigate threats linked to external state actors operating within the United States.

The severe prison term reflects the gravity of the charges and the federal judiciary's strict stance on acts directed against public officials by foreign entities.

stories.title: Armed Robbers Loot Gold and Cash Worth Millions in Karachi Incidents
stories.summary:
Law enforcement agencies in Karachi are investigating two major armed robberies where criminals made off with substantial amounts of cash and valuables. The first incident took place at a residential bungalow located in Block 6 of Gulistan-e-Jauhar, where a gang of five suspects targeted the occupants and fled with gold jewellery and cash.

According to police reports regarding the Gulistan-e-Jauhar break-in, three armed men forced their way inside the residence and held the inhabitants hostage. Two accomplices waited outside inside a vehicle, which investigators noted was fitted with a fake licence plate. Prior to executing the robbery, the suspects reportedly spent nearly an hour roaming the surrounding neighbourhood. After seizing the valuables, the three inside the house were picked up by their waiting partners, allowing all five to escape successfully. Authorities are actively pursuing leads to determine the identities of the suspects and trace the vehicle used in the getaway.

In a separate occurrence in the Liaquatabad area, armed individuals targeted a milk shop situated in the Super Market sector. CCTV footage capturing the crime has emerged, showing a single suspect initially entering the establishment and demanding money at gunpoint. Six additional accomplices subsequently arrived at the location to assist with the theft. A formal First Information Report has been registered with local police, and inquiries into both separate criminal operations are presently underway.

stories.title: South Korean President Lee Discusses Peace and Trade With Xi Jinping
stories.summary:
South Korean President Lee Jae Myung met with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday to discuss regional stability and economic collaboration. Speaking on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation gathering in Shenzhen, President Lee emphasized that ensuring peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula is vital for the strategic partnership between the two nations to mature. He also stated his desire to further develop an equal and mutually beneficial economic partnership with China.

In response to these remarks, Chinese President Xi Jinping indicated that Beijing is prepared to enhance communication and coordination with South Korea. Xi noted that this cooperation aims to maintain stability and ensure the smooth operation of global industrial and supply chains.

The high-level talks occurred amidst broader diplomatic activities regarding the region. US President Donald Trump has mentioned the possibility of meeting North Korean leader Kim Jong Un during his current trip to Asia, although officials have not confirmed any such encounter. China stated it possesses no information regarding a potential meeting between Trump and Kim.

Meanwhile, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio remarked on Wednesday that President Trump is prepared for dialogue with Pyongyang. However, Rubio clarified that this readiness does not guarantee a meeting will actually take place during the visit. These diplomatic discussions highlight ongoing international efforts to address security and stability concerns across the Korean Peninsula.

stories.title: Automated European Earthquake Alert System Triggers After Romania Tremor
stories.summary:
An overnight earthquake in the Vrancea activity zone of Romania triggered an automated network of mobile emergency alerts across 17 European nations. Localized sub-regional and crowdsourced automated early-warning systems, including Android, utilized initial sensor data to disseminate safety warnings to residents within a matter of seconds. Initial automated algorithms estimated the magnitude of the tremor at 6.5, but subsequent reviews and instrumentation by expert seismologists validated the final magnitude at 5.6.

Because the earthquake had a focus depth of approximately 140 kilometers, its energy spread across a notably large distance. Consequently, a series of minor shocks were felt in the immediate vicinity and across national borders into neighboring Moldova and Bulgaria.

Emergency services and local authorities throughout all of the impacted regions confirmed that there were no reported deaths, injuries, or structural damage to buildings and significant infrastructure. Despite the lack of physical destruction, emergency dispatchers did receive a small number of phone calls from residents experiencing anxiety and panic. Officials noted this public reaction as a clear illustration of the psychological impact that widespread automated alerts can have on local populations.

stories.title: Kozo Tashima Officially Enters Race for FIFA Presidency Against Gianni Infantino
stories.summary:
Kozo Tashima, Honorary President of the Japan Football Association, has officially submitted his candidacy for the presidency of FIFA. Tashima successfully secured the necessary endorsements from five national federations to challenge incumbent Gianni Infantino, who is currently seeking a fourth term leading global soccer's governing body. The Japan Football Association confirmed on Wednesday that it submitted a formal letter to FIFA nominating Tashima, making him the first Japanese candidate to ever run for the position. Tashima has served on the FIFA Council since 2015 and is a former Japan international player and youth coach.

The deadline for submitting nominations for the upcoming FIFA presidential election was set to close at 2259 GMT on Wednesday. The election vote will take place four months later at the 77th FIFA Congress, scheduled for March 18 in Rabat. Candidates running for the office must meet specific criteria, including having played an active role in football as a player or official within FIFA, a confederation, or a national association for two of the last five years, alongside obtaining at least five member association nominations.

Expressing gratitude to JFA President Tsuneyasu Miyamoto, the board members, and the international football associations that provided support, Tashima stated his intention to take on the challenge with a strong sense of mission. He aims to help FIFA evolve into a healthier, more trusted organization that contributes to the global development of the sport, though he did not publicly disclose which specific foreign associations joined the JFA in nominating him. A report from TV Asahi indicated that Tashima completed his application process early Wednesday morning.

Incumbent Gianni Infantino faces opposition in this election cycle following previous controversies, including an aborted attempt to bring private investors into a new commercial entity holding rights for major competitions like the World Cup, an initiative for which the Swiss official later apologized to the FIFA Council. In addition to Tashima and Infantino, other challengers in the race include former Switzerland captain Ramon Vega and French Football Federation President Philippe Diallo.

stories.title: Magnitude 5.9 Earthquake Strikes Indonesia's Flores Region
stories.summary:
An earthquake with a magnitude of 5.9 occurred in Indonesia’s Flores region on Wednesday. The German Research Centre for Geosciences reported the seismic activity.

According to the agency, the tremor struck at a shallow depth of 10 kilometers, which is equivalent to 6 miles.

stories.title: Pakistan Considers October Fuel Price Hike of Rs2.88 Per Unit
stories.summary:
Electricity consumers throughout Pakistan could face an extra cost of Rs2.88 per unit following a fuel price adjustment request for October. This proposed adjustment is anticipated to create a financial strain exceeding Rs35 billion for electricity users. The Central Power Purchasing Agency filed the petition with the National Electric Power Regulatory Authority, which has scheduled a formal hearing regarding the request for November 26.

Filing details show that national electricity generation reached 10.744 billion units in October, with 10.352 billion units delivered to distribution companies. Average generation costs hit Rs10.75 per unit for the month, exceeding the established reference cost of Rs7.86 per unit. K-Electric consumers are also expected to experience the impact of this price adjustment.

If the regulatory authority approves the application, consumers will see the additional charges reflected in their upcoming monthly bills. The final verdict on the tariff change rests with NEPRA following the November hearing. Meanwhile, the Power Division rejected recent media reports claiming an industrial tariff increase, explaining that the cited figure represented a marginal rate under the Incremental Consumption Package rather than an industrial tariff hike.

The Power Division further noted that overall industrial electricity tariffs have dropped by roughly Rs18.94 per unit, inclusive of all taxes, when compared to the rates active in March 2024. The adjustments continue to draw close attention from consumers and officials alike as the upcoming regulatory review approaches next week.

stories.title: Australian Dollar Hovers Near Ten-Month Lows Amid Wage Jump
stories.summary:
The Australian dollar traded near ten-month lows as equity sell-offs weighed on the currency, while a stronger-than-expected rise in wages elevated the importance of upcoming employment statistics. The Aussie slipped 0.1 percent to $0.6726 after declining for six straight sessions and hitting a ten-month low of $0.6720. Minimal support exists until the year-to-date low of $0.6662.

Official figures revealed that domestic wages expanded at their fastest pace in nearly three years during the September quarter. This growth supports earlier aggressive interest rate increases intended to curb inflation, although the data predated the month's fifth rate rise. Citi Australia analysts noted that elevated business cost pressures and excess domestic demand complicate the situation for policymakers.

Labor market data is anticipated to show a 25,000 job increase for October, with the unemployment rate steady at 4.7 percent, marking a five-year high. Should unemployment tighten further to 4.6 percent alongside strong employment growth, the Reserve Bank of Australia board might consider an additional 25-basis-point rate hike. Swaps currently indicate a 75 percent probability that interest rates have peaked, with some policy easing expected by late 2027.

In New Zealand, the kiwi dollar remained steady at $0.5497 following an overnight decline to $0.5483, its lowest level since March 2020. Financial markets price in an 80 percent probability that the Reserve Bank of New Zealand will raise interest rates by a quarter percentage point to 3 percent by the end of next year.

stories.title: Malaysian Palm Oil Futures Extend Losses Amid Weak Rival Oils
stories.summary:
Malaysian palm oil futures dropped during early trading sessions, marking a second consecutive day of losses. The downward trend was primarily driven by weaker performance in rival edible oils and declining crude oil prices across global markets.

The benchmark palm oil contract for delivery in February on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange fell by 54 ringgit, translating to a 1.22 percent decrease. This brought the trading price down to 4,382 ringgit, or approximately $1,071.39, per metric ton during the early hours of trade.

The persistent decline highlights ongoing pressures from related commodity markets impacting the vegetable oil sector. Traders and analysts continue to monitor external price movements in competing oils and energy markets to gauge near-term direction for the benchmark contract.

The drop affects overall market sentiment on the exchange as participants react to shifting regional supply and demand fundamentals. Further developments in energy and rival oil prices are expected to dictate the trajectory of palm oil futures in upcoming sessions.

stories.title: US Doctors Warn of Measles Resurgence Amid Dropping Vaccination Rates
stories.summary:
Medical professionals across the United States are confronting a resurgence of measles, a disease many previously viewed as historical due to decades of high immunization coverage. The Pan American Health Organization reported that the United States has lost its measles-free status, with over 5,400 cases documented nationally this year. Pediatric infectious disease specialists describe encountering the illness as akin to seeing a ghost from the past.

In Utah, specialist Trahern W. Jones noted over 500 cases in his state alone and believes actual totals are significantly undercounted. The highly contagious virus generates recognizable red spots, high fevers, and severe respiratory symptoms. Physicians emphasize that infections frequently lead to dangerous complications such as pneumonia, brain inflammation, and permanent neurological damage, noting that measles severely harms the immune system.

In Pennsylvania, pediatrician Jessica Ericson reported treating around 30 patients since the spring amid more than 1,500 cases statewide, heavily concentrated in an Amish population that avoids vaccines for religious reasons. Seven fatalities have been recorded in the state, all involving unvaccinated patients. Experts point out that fevers associated with measles are far more extreme than those caused by typical viral illnesses.

Medical experts attribute the spread to falling vaccination rates driven by religious exemptions and widespread misinformation. Specialists have criticized figures like Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. for amplifying unfounded safety concerns regarding immunizations. Doctors stress that widespread community vaccination remains essential to prevent transmissions and severe, potentially fatal outcomes.

stories.title: Australian Shares Extend Losses for Fifth Consecutive Session
stories.summary:
Australian shares dropped for a fifth consecutive day on Wednesday, with the S&P/ASX 200 index falling 0.2% to reach 8,883.2 by 2304 GMT. Over the prior four sessions, the benchmark index lost approximately 3%. The primary driver of the downturn was weakness in the banking sector, where financial stocks extended losses by 0.9%. This followed the Reserve Bank of Australia’s November policy meeting, during which policymakers indicated that recent rate hikes were necessary because inflation risks remained skewed upward and financial conditions were insufficiently restrictive. Consequently, the "Big Four" banks experienced declines ranging between 0.8% and 1.5%. Market participants are now awaiting upcoming Australian employment data scheduled for release on Thursday to gauge the central bank's future policy trajectory, noting that the RBA views the softening labor market as a source of inflationary pressure.

In contrast, mining stocks managed a 1.4% rebound, threatening to break a four-day losing streak that had wiped out over 10% of their value due to sluggish iron ore and copper prices. Major mining companies BHP and Rio Tinto posted share price gains of 1.7% and 0.1%, respectively, though sector sentiment has recently been constrained by weak Chinese economic data and concerns surrounding artificial intelligence spending.

Technology stocks experienced a notable downward trend, sliding as much as 2.2% to touch their lowest point in over a week. This movement mirrored overnight losses on the Nasdaq as markets braced for Nvidia's upcoming earnings report. During extended trading, Nvidia shares rose 4.5% after the AI chip manufacturer issued sales forecasts that exceeded Wall Street expectations. Meanwhile, Chairman Harvey Jones clarified that the company would not rehire co-founder Jensen Huang as chief executive officer.

The broader economic context underscores how sensitive regional markets remain to central bank signals and global technology sector developments. Investors continue to monitor inflation metrics and labor statistics closely to predict whether the RBA will maintain its current stance or pause its tightening cycle. Meanwhile, commodity price fluctuations continue to heavily influence domestic mining valuations across the Australian exchange.

stories.title: Japan's Nikkei Slips Amid US AI Concerns and Nvidia Leadership Volatility
stories.summary:
Japan’s Nikkei average dropped during Wednesday's trading session, erasing earlier gains of up to 1.3% to close down 0.72% by 0220 GMT. The broader Topix index similarly declined, falling 1.02% to 3,800.96. The market downturn was primarily driven by ongoing concerns regarding artificial intelligence development in the United States and leadership uncertainty at Nvidia, which overshadowed the chipmaker's strong financial outlook.

Nvidia, widely regarded as a key bellwether for the global AI sector, reported quarterly revenue exceeding market expectations in its first earnings release since the abrupt departure of CEO Jensen Huang earlier in the month. Despite the robust financial results, investor sentiment was rattled by leadership signals rejecting a "Stand With Jensen" campaign from Huang's allies, alongside reports from the Wall Street Journal indicating that a regulatory probe into Nvidia was underway. Kazuaki Shimada, chief strategist at IwaiCosmo Securities, noted that momentum sparked by Nvidia's forecasts was short-lived due to anxieties surrounding Huang's future and potential slowdowns in US data center construction, alongside upcoming developments regarding Anthropic's initial public offering.

Locally in Japan, technology-related equities suffered visible losses. Tokyo Electron fell 2.73%, memory chip manufacturer Kioxia dropped 2.44%, and Fujikura, which produces fiber-optic cables for data centers, lost 2.66%. Financial institutions also weighed heavily on the Topix, with major lenders Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group each declining by more than 2%, while Mizuho Financial Group fell 1.25%. Additionally, conglomerate Rakuten Group dropped 5% after its brokerage division warned that customer information might have been compromised following unauthorized third-party access to its computer systems.

Market breadth on the Tokyo Stock Exchange prime market reflected the widespread sell-off. Out of more than 1,500 listed stocks, only 19% advanced, while 77% declined and 2% remained flat. The downturn illustrates how deeply interconnected Japanese equities are with US tech sector governance and regulatory scrutiny.

stories.title: Pakistani Police Officer Abducted and Tortured to Death in Bannu
stories.summary:
A police constable named Javed was abducted and tortured to death by unidentified armed men near Taziri Chowk in Bannu on Wednesday. According to local law enforcement, the fatal incident occurred within the operational boundaries of the Basia Khel police station. Police authorities have initiated an investigation into the attack and launched efforts to identify and apprehend the perpetrators.

The killing follows a series of similar violent incidents targeting law enforcement personnel in the Bannu district over recent months. Just a day prior, Head Constable Zahid Khan of the Elite Force was shot and killed near an Afghan refugee camp while performing his duties at the Central Jail. Previous months saw multiple targeted attacks, including the June 29 shooting of Constable Umar Niaz Khan after he was pulled from a rickshaw, the September assassination of Elite Force personnel Ahmadullah at a Peepal Bazaar shop, and the October 15 killing of District Security Branch Head Constable Raqeeb Khan on Circular Road. Furthermore, October 31 marked the killings of Counter-Terrorism Department driver Constable Sadiq Zaman and Bannu Police Lines Head Constable Ziaullah, the latter of whom was abducted near Baran Dam.

Beyond targeted assassinations, police posts and individual officers in Bannu have frequently faced armed assaults and drone attacks, resulting in injuries and triggering localized security operations. In response to the persistent security challenges, Section 144 has remained in force across Bannu since November 14, imposing various restrictions aimed at preserving public order. Security forces continue their targeted operations to dismantle terrorist networks operating within the region.

stories.title: Cricket Australia Rejects New Ball-Tampering Probe but Announces Player Forum
stories.summary:
Cricket Australia (CA) announced on Wednesday that it will not reopen an investigation into the 2018 ball-tampering scandal in Cape Town, opting instead to establish an independent forum for players and staff to share their perspectives as a "circuit breaker." The controversy was reignited the previous week following the release of an autobiography by former Australian cricketer Usman Khawaja, in which he alleged that the entire team was aware of the plot to use sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball. Current captain Pat Cummins has strongly denied any personal involvement.

An official CA investigation conducted at the time concluded that only captain Steve Smith, vice-captain David Warner, and player Cameron Bancroft were cognizant of the plan, leading to their dismissal from the team and subsequent bans. Warner recently criticized CA's initial inquiry as shoddy and claimed not all players were interviewed, though he has expressed support for Khawaja's account. Speaking in Hobart ahead of Australia's one-day match against England, CA Chief Executive Todd Greenberg defended the original investigation as complete and maintained that its findings must remain confidential. Interim Chairman David Boon stated that the newly proposed forum, likely to be overseen by a former judge, is designed to allow involved individuals to have their voices heard without imposing any new sanctions.

While Cricket Australia hopes to conclude the process within a month, the initiative has met with mixed reactions from key figures. Warner advocated for an open inquiry focused on transparency and cultural accountability rather than penalties. Similarly, Khawaja welcomed the creation of a safe dialogue space but raised concerns regarding board control over what information ultimately gets released to the public. Greenberg emphasized that the forum is intended to help the sport move past the enduring pain of the 2018 incident rather than to appease any specific individual.

stories.title: Democrat Mary Peltola Wins Alaska Senate Seat, Securing 56-44 Majority
stories.summary:
Democrat Mary Peltola secured victory in Alaska's U.S. Senate race, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan. Projected by U.S. media, Peltola's win gives her party its ninth midterm election flip and grants Democrats a 56-44 Senate majority, marking their largest majority since 2009. She captured 50 percent of the first-place votes compared to Sullivan's 46 percent, successfully clearing the threshold to avoid additional rounds under the state's ranked-choice voting system. The outcome sets up a potential two-year deadlock between Congress and President Donald Trump, who won Alaska by 13 percentage points in 2024.

The contest was the final uncalled race in the Senate. Despite Donald Trump's prior performance in the state, voter frustration concerning the high cost of living and Alaska's independent political streak brought the seat into play for Democrats. Following the media projections, Peltola shared her commitment on X to fight corporate greed and lower costs for Alaskans.

The election process drew controversy due to allegations that Democrats helped recruit Dan J. Sullivan Jr., a retired schoolteacher running as an independent, to act as a spoiler and confuse voters. Republicans unsuccessfully urged the Alaska Supreme Court to remove him, arguing he was not a good-faith candidate. Although Peltola's campaign denied involvement, Republican Governor Mike Dunleavy initiated a state investigation into possible perjury, and the U.S. Justice Department launched a criminal investigation.

U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche characterized the reported recruitment effort as fraud. The Justice Department has issued over 140 subpoenas, letters, and notices regarding the probe, though these actions do not indicate guilt. Alaska's isolated communities also contributed to an unusually lengthy vote count in the state's final uncalled Senate race.

stories.title: سوات اور گردونواح میں زلزلے کے جھٹکے، شدت 4.5 ریکارڈ کی گئی
stories.summary:
سوات اور اس کے اردگرد کے علاقوں میں زلزلے کے جھٹکے محسوس کیے گئے ہیں جن کی شدت زلزلہ پیما مرکز کے مطابق 4.5 ریکارڈ کی گئی۔ اس زلزلے کی گہرائی 216 کلومیٹر ریکارڈ کی گئی جبکہ زلزلے کا مرکز ہندوکش کا پہاڑی سلسلہ تھا۔

زلزلے کے یہ جھٹکے محسوس ہونے کے بعد متاثرہ علاقوں میں خوف و ہراس پھیل گیا اور لوگ کلمہ طیبہ کا ورد کرتے ہوئے اپنے گھروں سے باہر کھلے آسمان تلے نکل آئے۔

اس قدرتی آفت کے حوالے سے زلزلہ پیما مرکز نے ضروری اعداد و شمار جاری کیے ہیں جن سے زلزلے کے مقام اور گہرائی کا تعین کیا گیا ہے۔

زلزلے کے فوری بعد شہریوں کی جانب سے حفاظتی تدبیر کے طور پر کھلے مقامات کا رخ کیا گیا تاکہ کسی بھی ممکنہ نقصان سے محفوظ رہا جا سکے।

stories.title: Aamir Jamal Praises Seamer-Friendly Pitches in Pakistan Cricket
stories.summary:
Pakistan fast-bowling all-rounder Aamir Jamal has expressed strong approval for the shift toward seamer-friendly Test pitches in Pakistan, calling it a major positive development for the country's cricket. Speaking to the media at the Rawalpindi International Cricket Stadium, Jamal discussed the benefits of preparing conditions that offer strong assistance to seam and bounce, noting that such pitches enhance Pakistan's home advantage during the World Test Championship cycle.

The remarks came after the opening day of the second Test against Sri Lanka, where Pakistan captain Babar Azam won the toss and elected to field. The home team's pace attack swiftly dismantled Sri Lanka, bowling out the tourists for just 98 runs in 35.3 overs, which marked their fifth-lowest first-innings total against Pakistan. Jamal led the bowling effort by taking 3 wickets for 24 runs in 5.3 overs, while fellow pacemen Mohammad Abbas and Razaullah claimed three wickets each to account for six dismissals between them.

Jamal emphasized that utilizing pitches that consistently assist seamers will also improve the preparation of both local and international bowlers for foreign tours. Historically, flat and batter-friendly surfaces in Pakistan have blunted the team's traditional bowling strengths.

Capitalizing on their bowlers' dominant opening-day performance, Pakistan solidified their position by the end of the second day. Openers Azan Awais and Tayyab Arif established a solid 80-run partnership against the visiting pace duo, allowing Pakistan to build a commanding lead.

stories.title: Xi and Putin Meet in Shenzhen Ahead of Trilateral Summit with Trump
stories.summary:
Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin held discussions in Shenzhen on Wednesday, marking their fifth meeting of the year. The bilateral talks precede a historic three-way summit scheduled for Thursday in the southern Chinese city, which will include U.S. President Donald Trump. The upcoming trilateral meeting has raised concerns among European nations and Kyiv that major powers could determine the fate of Ukraine and establish new spheres of influence.

While Washington initially indicated that Ukraine would not be part of the agenda, President Trump later stated that the topic would be addressed. Beijing stated that the leaders would engage in in-depth exchanges regarding world peace and strategic stability during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) gathering. Additional topics slated for discussion include the Iran war and nuclear disarmament, particularly after a U.S.-Russian atomic weapons treaty expired in February. Beijing has maintained that the U.S. and Russia must reduce their larger nuclear arsenals before it enters into talks concerning its smaller stockpile.

Ahead of the meetings, Putin addressed the APEC gathering, describing the upcoming trilateral summit as highly useful and emphasizing the need for unity and dialogue over division and ultimatums. He also claimed that Western sanctions imposed since his 2022 invasion of Ukraine had failed to destroy Russia's economy. Meanwhile, Xi called for enhanced international cooperation on artificial intelligence and free trade, pledging deep-seated reforms beginning with tariff reductions.

President Trump arrived in Shenzhen following a stop in the Philippines, where he met with Quad leaders—representing Australia, Japan, and India—and attended an Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit. Trump's regional engagements have been accompanied by ongoing trade tensions and protests, alongside new U.S. rules requiring special licenses for advanced AI chip transfers to certain Southeast Asian nations due to diversion risks.

stories.title: ایرانی فوج کی کویت کے علی السلم بیس پر حملے کی تصدیق
stories.summary:
ایرانی فوج نے تصدیق کی ہے کہ اس نے کویت میں امریکی افواج کے زیرِ استعمال علی السالم ایئر بیس کو ڈرون حملوں کا نشانہ بنایا ہے۔ حملے کا ہدف امریکی فوجی تنصیبات، فضائی دفاعی نظام اور ڈرون و میزائل لانچر تھے۔ بدھ کی صبح جاری ہونے والے بیان میں ایران نے واضح کیا کہ وہ اپنی سلامتی کے دفاع میں کسی دباؤ کے سامنے نہیں جھکے گا۔

اس کارروائی سے پہلے کویتی فوج نے حملہ آور ڈرونز کا مقابلہ کرنے کے لیے اپنا فضائی دفاعی نظام فعال کرنے کا اعلان کیا تھا۔ کویت کے علاوہ بحرین میں بھی فضائی حملوں کے خطرے سے متعلق انتباہات جاری کیے گئے اور دھماکوں کی آوازیں سنی گئیں۔ ایرانی پاسدارانِ انقلاب کے مطابق بحرین میں شیخ عیسیٰ ایئر بیس پر امریکی افواج کے ریڈار نظام کو نشانہ بنایا گیا۔

دوسری جانب بحرینی حکام کا کہنا ہے کہ ان کے فضائی دفاعی نظام نے تمام حملہ آور اہداف کو تباہ کر دیا۔ بحرین کی وزارتِ خارجہ نے ان حملوں کو خودمختاری کی خلافورزی قرار دیتے ہوئے سلامتی کونسل سے کارروائی کا مطالبہ کیا ہے۔ دریں اثنا، امریکی جنگی طیاروں نے آبنائے ہرمز میں واقع ایرانی جزیرے قشم پر پاسدارانِ انقلاب کی میزائل لانچنگ سائٹ کو نشانہ بنایا۔

امریکی صدر ڈونلڈ ٹرمپ نے خبردار کیا ہے کہ واشنگٹن یا امریکی مفادات کے خلاف کسی بھی خطرے کا جواب بے مثال ہوگا۔ دریں اثنا، ایران نے واشنگٹن پر ممکنہ کیمیکل ڈرٹی بم حملے کی خبروں کو مسترد کرتے ہوئے انہیں بے بنیاد قرار دیا ہے۔ اس دوران خلیج میں کشیدگی میں مزید اضافہ ہو گیا ہے۔

stories.title: Xi, Putin Meet in Shenzhen Ahead of Trilateral Summit with Trump
stories.summary:
Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met in Shenzhen on Wednesday for discussions ahead of a scheduled three-way summit with US President Donald Trump. The upcoming trilateral talks have raised international concerns that these major powers might address the conflict in Ukraine without the participation of Kyiv or Europe, potentially establishing twenty-first-century spheres of influence. While Washington previously indicated that Ukraine would not be part of the agenda, Trump subsequently stated that it would be discussed.

In addition to regional conflicts, the leaders were anticipated to cover topics such as the ongoing war in Iran, nuclear disarmament, energy, and finance. Beijing maintains that the United States and Russia must reduce their larger nuclear stockpiles before engaging in discussions regarding its own arsenal. This meeting marks the fifth time Xi and Putin have interacted this year. Speaking at the APEC summit, Putin criticized Western sanctions as ineffective and emphasized the necessity of dialogue amid rising military and political risks.

Meanwhile, Donald Trump remained in the Philippines following a meeting with Quad leaders Australia, Japan, and India. During his regional tour, Trump engaged in trade tensions with China, asserting that the US would match Chinese rare-earths production within ten months. Furthermore, Washington announced new regulations requiring special licenses for advanced AI chips shipped to several Southeast Asian nations due to diversion risks, prompting responses from regional hubs like Singapore.

The broader APEC and ASEAN gatherings have highlighted significant friction over unilateral trade policies and tariffs. Chinese Premier Li Qiang criticized protectionist measures, while other international figures, including Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada’s Mark Carney, discussed reducing economic reliance on the United States. The diplomatic engagements in Shenzhen continue to shape global economic and security dynamics as major world leaders navigate complex geopolitical alliances and trade disputes.

stories.title: Malaysia Opens Long-Term Residency Programme for Pakistani Nationals
stories.summary:
Malaysia has officially opened opportunities for Pakistani nationals to apply for long-term residency through its Malaysia My Second Home (MM2H) initiative. This announcement was made by the Consul General of Malaysia in Karachi, Yunus Ibrahim, during a press briefing held at the Consulate General of Malaysia.

The initiative, frequently characterized as Malaysia's Golden Visa scheme, grants qualifying foreign nationals residency privileges lasting anywhere from five to twenty years. The Malaysian government has recently restructured and revised the programme into distinct categories to offer flexible options for international applicants looking to establish residential ties.

Through this scheme, eligible Pakistani applicants can take advantage of Malaysia's infrastructure, lifestyle, and investment environment. The initiative is also intended to foster stronger people-to-people connections and enhance social, economic, and cultural relations between Pakistan and Malaysia.

During the media briefing, Consul General Yunus Ibrahim formally announced the appointment of Greenland Travels (Pvt) Ltd as the designated authorized representative for the MM2H programme within Pakistan. Interested applicants must meet specific eligibility criteria, financial prerequisites, and immigration guidelines set forth for each category of the residency scheme.

stories.title: Commerce Ministry to Support HBL in Expanding International Trade Links
stories.summary:
Pakistan's Ministry of Commerce has committed to supporting Habib Bank Limited (HBL) in bolstering trade-financing and banking connections with key international partners. Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan reached this agreement during a meeting with an HBL delegation led by President and CEO Muhammad Nassir Salim.

The discussions focused on SME financing, digital banking, export facilitation, and broadening Pakistan's trade reach in major global markets. Specifically, the Ministry of Commerce will assist HBL in strengthening financial linkages with Bangladesh, China, the Maldives, and Sri Lanka to streamline cross-border transactions and improve bilateral trade.

During the talks, Jam Kamal emphasized the critical need to transition Pakistan's informal small and medium-sized enterprise sector into the documented economy. He noted that formalization is vital for improving access to institutional financing, ensuring compliance with international quality standards, and boosting export competitiveness. Both sides also addressed the challenges financial institutions face when dealing with undocumented businesses.

Additionally, the officials reviewed broader strategies to diversify Pakistan's exports across regions such as Africa, Southeast Asia, and the Middle East. The meeting concluded with an agreement to maintain close coordination between the ministry and HBL to advance financial inclusion, investment growth, and commercial engagement abroad.

stories.title: Indiana Fever Guard Sophie Cunningham Shares BTS Photos from SI Shoot
stories.summary:
Indiana Fever guard Sophie Cunningham is actively engaged in media endeavors and high-profile offseason events following the conclusion of her second year with the team. During the 2026 WNBA regular season, Cunningham played 43 games, averaging 7.9 points, 2.3 rebounds, and 1.2 assists in 22.2 minutes per contest while shooting 46 percent from the field and 41.9 percent from beyond the arc. The Fever finished with a 28-16 record, secured the sixth playoff seed, and were eliminated in the first round by the top-seeded Las Vegas Aces.

Away from the basketball court, the 30-year-old athlete co-hosts the "No Hesitation" podcast alongside trainer Drew Hanlen. Her offseason schedule has also featured appearances at notable sports events, including the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix in Austin and NASCAR’s Season Finale 400 in Miami. Most recently, Cunningham traveled to New York City to participate in the 2027 Sports Illustrated Swim Search casting competition, marking her second engagement with the magazine following her debut in the 2026 issue.

To share the experience with her followers, Cunningham posted behind-the-scenes clips and photographs on her Instagram Stories from the photoshoot. One of her outfits featured black jeans, a black T-shirt, a black leather jacket, and heels, accompanied by a caption acknowledging the publication. Her previous appearance was photographed by Katherine Goguen at the South Seas Resort on Captiva Island, Florida.

As she approaches the 2027 season as an unrestricted free agent, Cunningham has not yet signed with a new team, though a return to the Indiana Fever remains a distinct possibility. Her dual involvement in professional basketball and prominent media activities establishes her as one of the most visible personalities in the league.

stories.title: Ukraine Strikes Crimea Bridge and Kyiv Crossings Amid Intensifying Russian Attacks
stories.summary:
A section of the road-and-rail bridge connecting Russia to the annexed Crimean peninsula was severely damaged and left lying in rubble after a brazen overnight missile strike by Ukraine. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky described the operation as unprecedented and a justified response to continuous Russian barrages targeting Ukrainian infrastructure as the conflict grinds through another winter. Road traffic across the Crimea bridge was completely halted following the attack.

Simultaneously, Moscow launched intense ballistic missile and drone strikes targeting key infrastructure in Kyiv, hitting both the Northern and Southern bridges across the Dnipro River. The strikes caused massive morning rush-hour traffic gridlock and disrupted essential heating and water supplies in parts of the capital. Russian authorities confirmed the hits on the capital's bridges, while Kyiv Mayor Vitali Klitschko shared video footage showing extensive debris on the Northern Bridge before traffic partially resumed on the Southern structure.

Amid the escalating winter hostilities, diplomatic efforts led by the United States to end the war have not achieved any breakthrough. Meanwhile, Russian Foreign Minister Sergei Lavrov stated that Moscow is aware of French troops operating inside Ukraine to train personnel and maintain equipment, calling the deployment direct participation in the war. France strongly rejected Lavrov's claims as absurd, with deputy defense minister Alice Rufo clarifying that a very limited number of French trainers are deployed without any combat role or intention to engage in coercive actions.

The ongoing conflict continues to heavily impact civilian life and regional stability, with winter weather compounding hardships across Ukraine. The attacks underscore the relentless escalation in aerial bombardments as both sides maintain firm stances, leaving diplomatic resolutions distant while economic and infrastructure strains mount across the region.

stories.title: PSX KSE-100 Index Sheds Over 900 Points Amid Broad Selling Pressure
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Stock Exchange experienced a sharp downturn as the benchmark KSE-100 Index shed over 900 points during the opening minutes of trading. Selling pressure was widely observed across key economic sectors, including cement, commercial banks, oil and gas exploration companies, oil marketing companies, power generation, and refineries. Prominent index-heavy stocks such as ARL, HUBCO, MARI, OGDC, PPL, POL, PSO, MCB, MEBL, and UBL all traded in negative territory.

The latest market decline followed a previous session marked by broad-based selling and profit-taking at higher levels, which had reversed an early market rally supported by declining international oil prices. During that prior session, the benchmark index had fallen by 665.21 points to close at 177,517.74 points. Compounding these local market jitters, the State Bank of Pakistan issued a cautionary statement warning that evolving external and domestic risks could pose significant challenges to the macroeconomic outlook and impact projected economic outcomes.

The central bank specifically highlighted potential threats stemming from a prolonged conflict in the Middle East and extreme weather events associated with El Niño. These domestic concerns unfolded against a mixed international backdrop where Asian stocks advanced following strong sales forecasts from chipmaker Nvidia, even as Wall Street indices had logged consecutive session losses prior to those earnings reports.

stories.title: Chinese Scientist Fired Following Cover-Up of Child Death in Gene-Editing Trial
stories.summary:
A prominent Chinese neuroscientist has been dismissed from his position after a government investigation revealed he concealed the death of a young girl during an experimental gene-editing trial. Zilong Qiu, who served as the lead researcher and deputy director of the Songjiang Research Institute at Shanghai Jiao Tong University, faced termination following a joint investigation by outlets Science and Retraction Watch. State broadcaster CCTV confirmed the dismissal based on a statement released by Shanghai authorities.

The six-year-old girl died last year after undergoing experimental gene therapy intended to correct a non-life-threatening medical condition. Investigators discovered that Qiu completely omitted any mention of the child's tragic death in a published research paper that appeared in the prestigious journal Nature. The study, cited by state media, was published on February 18.

In addition to losing his administrative post, Qiu was handed a five-year suspension from participating in scientific projects. Furthermore, authorities entered his name into an official database for serious breaches of research integrity. The case has drawn significant scrutiny regarding ethical standards and transparency in advanced genetic research trials.

stories.title: رحمان گل عرف مرید بلوچ کالعدم بی ایل اے کے نئے کمانڈر مقرر
stories.summary:
کالعدم علیحدگی پسند تنظیم بلوچ لبریشن آرمی نے رحمان گل عرف مرید بلوچ کو تنظیم کا نیا کمانڈر ان چیف منتخب کرنے کا اعلان کیا ہے۔ ان کی یہ تقرری بشیر زیب بلوچ کی جگہ عمل میں آئی ہے، جنہیں نومبر کے اوائل میں اس عہدے سے ہٹا دیا گیا تھا۔ رحمان گل اسلم بلوچ کی قیادت میں بی ایل اے کی تشکیل نو کے بعد تنظیم کے تیسرے کمانڈر ان چیف بنے ہیں۔

رحمان گل کا تعلق نوشکی کے کلی مینگل سے ہے اور وہ ایک معروف مینگل خاندان سے تعلق رکھتے ہیں۔ ان کے والد نوشکی سے آزاد امیدوار کے طور پر الیکشن لڑ چکے ہیں، جبکہ ممتاز شاعر گل خان نصیر ان کے قریبی رشتہ دار تھے۔ رحمان گل نے پشاور یونیورسٹی سے بی اے کی ڈگری حاصل کی اور سنہ 2002 میں پاکستانی فوج میں کمیشنڈ آفیسر کی حیثیت سے شمولیت اختیار کی۔

فوج میں آٹھ سال تک خدمات انجام دینے کے بعد سنہ 2010 میں کیپٹن کے عہدے سے مستعفی ہو کر وہ کالعدم بی ایل اے میں شامل ہو گئے۔ انہوں نے بولان میں اسلم بلوچ کے ماتحت کام کیا اور بعد میں مجید بریگیڈ کے سربراہ بنے۔ محکمہ داخلہ بلوچستان کے مطابق ان کے خلاف سو سے زائد مقدمات درج ہیں اور ان کی گرفتاری پر 25 کروڑ روپے کا انعام مقرر ہے۔

تجزیہ کاروں کے مطابق یہ تبدیلی تنظیم کی بنیادی ساخت میں تبدیلی کی بجائے ایک تکنیکی اور حربی تبدیلی ہے۔ سکیورٹی ماہرین کا کہنا ہے کہ رحمان گل کا فوجی پس منظر ہونے کی وجہ سے پاکستانی سکیورٹی اداروں کو مزید الرٹ رہنے کی ضرورت ہے، کیونکہ حالیہ مہینوں میں سکیورٹی فورسز کی جانب سے انٹیلیجنس بیسڈ آپریشنز میں اضافہ دیکھا گیا ہے۔

stories.title: Pakistan and Saudi Firm Sign MoU to Explore $30 Billion Gas Pipeline
stories.summary:
Pakistan and Saudi Arabia have signed a Memorandum of Understanding to jointly assess the feasibility of developing a massive gas pipeline project alongside an LNG terminal at Gwadar. The proposed infrastructure initiative carries an estimated total investment ranging between $25 billion and $30 billion. The agreement was finalized between Pakistan's state-owned Inter State Gas Systems, operating under the Petroleum Division, and Delta Energy Saudi, a company affiliated with the Delta International Group.

The signing ceremony took place under the auspices of the Special Investment Facilitation Council and was attended by senior representatives from the SIFC, the Petroleum Division, ISGS, and Delta Energy Saudi. According to the proposed plans, the pipeline will originate in Turkmenistan, pass through Afghanistan, enter Pakistan near Chaman, traverse Balochistan, and ultimately terminate at Gwadar where an LNG terminal is planned. The project design also allows for future expansions to connect additional locations throughout the country.

The ambitious energy project is intended to significantly strengthen Pakistan's national energy security, diversify its natural gas supply sources, and enhance overall regional connectivity and economic cooperation. In a separate development highlighted during discussions, the Consul General of Malaysia in Karachi, Yunus Ibrahim, announced that Malaysia is offering Pakistani nationals long-term residency options through its Malaysia My Second Home program, providing residency privileges ranging from five to twenty years.

stories.title: Saudi Arabia’s Delta Energy Signs Accord to Explore Pakistan Infrastructure
stories.summary:
Saudi Arabian energy firm Delta Energy Saudi has signed an agreement with Pakistan’s Inter State Gas Systems to examine the development of energy infrastructure in Pakistan. The proposed investment carries an estimated value of about $30 billion. The announcement was made in a joint statement issued on Tuesday.

The initiative will evaluate a natural gas pipeline entering Pakistan through its western border and reaching toward the Arabian Sea port of Gwadar in the south-west. Furthermore, the plan will examine a potential extension to the eastern border, alongside liquefied natural gas facilities, gas processing and storage, and export terminals. Another proposed element is a pipeline running from Chaman on the Afghan border across Pakistan toward the Indian border near Fazilka.

Delta Energy characterized this route as a core strategic commitment that requires formal agreements with both Pakistani and Indian authorities. Potential supplies could come from Afghanistan’s Kashk gas concession and other resources. The companies noted that this framework operates separately from the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India project and does not rely on Turkmenistan.

The agreement establishes an evaluation framework rather than a final investment decision or a commitment to finance or construct the facilities. Plans for bringing gas into Pakistan via alternative pipelines have faced years of delays.

stories.title: Israeli Attacks Across Gaza Kill Six People Including Young Child
stories.summary:
Israeli military actions across the Gaza Strip resulted in six deaths on Tuesday, according to local hospitals and the territory's civil defence agency. The casualties included a six-year-old boy, as fighting continues despite a ceasefire that began in October 2025 following two years of conflict.

Civil defence spokesman Mahmoud Bassal reported that six people were killed and several injured by Israeli fire. Among the incidents, a strike in Deir el-Balah in central Gaza killed a 21-year-old and a six-year-old child named Iyas al-Namnam, whose death was confirmed by Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza. In northern Gaza, a drone bombing near the Jabalia camp killed two individuals, while Al-Shifa hospital confirmed two additional deaths in southern Gaza from bombing and live fire.

The Israeli military stated it was reviewing the reports, noted it struck several terrorists on Tuesday, and reported no awareness of any six-year-old killed by its operations. More than 1,600 Palestinians have died since the ceasefire started, based on figures from the Hamas-run health ministry.

Separately, the United Nations migration agency warned of potential hypothermia deaths among displaced Palestinians ahead of winter. Heavy rains have flooded tents housing displaced populations, and a nine-month-old infant recently died from suspected hypothermia. Karl Baker, head of the International Organisation for Migration's Gaza programme, stated that the agency faces a $173 million funding shortfall and highlighted that roughly 100,000 tents are awaiting entry through crossing points hindered by security checks.

stories.title: University of Minnesota Offers Free Online Food Safety Training Programme
stories.summary:
The University of Minnesota Extension in the United States has introduced a free online training course focused on Good Agricultural Practices and Farm Food Safety Planning. The educational program is designed for farmers, agriculture students, food science professionals, and individuals working within the agricultural sector.

According to Dairy Cattle Farmers Association Pakistan, the course aims to improve participants' comprehension of internationally recognized food safety standards. It also covers the practical steps required for the safe production, handling, and distribution of agricultural items from farms to consumer markets. Knowledge of these practices has grown increasingly vital due to global demands for food quality, hygiene, traceability, and sustainability.

Titled Good Agricultural Practices Training and Food Safety Plan, the online session is scheduled for December 7, 2026. The curriculum targets students, graduates, and professionals across agronomy, horticulture, agriculture, food safety, and agricultural economics.

For Pakistan, raising awareness of international standards helps enhance agricultural product quality, supply-chain management, and export competitiveness. DCFA Pakistan shared the announcement strictly for public awareness and educational purposes, noting that applicants must verify registration details directly through the official University of Minnesota Extension website.

stories.title: FBR Chairman Announces New Online Tax Refund System Starting in December
stories.summary:
Federal Board of Revenue Chairman Rashid Mahmood Langrial announced on Tuesday that a new online system to process pending tax refund claims for exporters will become operational next month. Speaking to the business community at the Lahore Chamber of Commerce and Industry, Langrial stated that the platform will enable online document submission and processing within defined timelines.

In addition to the refund system, the FBR chief stated that a dedicated online hearing room for customs valuation cases will open in Lahore. This facility will allow Lahore-based importers to handle their cases locally rather than traveling to Karachi. Langrial also noted that tax authorities expect to issue 30 percent more refunds this year compared to the previous year and mentioned that proposals to further empower the Director of Customs Valuation in Lahore will be evaluated.

Addressing complaints regarding customs valuation irregularities, Langrial assured attendees that senior officers will conduct daily hearings in Lahore to review grievances on merit. He also discussed ongoing government support for small and medium-sized enterprises and stated that the FBR remains open to reviewing feedback from various business sectors regarding the fixed tax scheme.

During the meeting, LCCI President Ali Hussam Asghar emphasized the need for regular cooperation and consultation between the FBR and the business community. He urged that tax policies should prioritize creating an enabling environment for industrial expansion, job creation, and investment alongside revenue collection.

stories.title: ICC Programme Excludes Pakistan from Hosting Major Cricket Events Until 2031
stories.summary:
The International Cricket Council has unveiled its activity schedule for the 2028-2035 cycle, leaving Pakistan without hosting rights for any major tournament until at least 2031. The announcement cements India’s influence in world cricket, with the ICC led by chairman Jay Shah, a former secretary of the Board of Control for Cricket in India, and chief executive officer Sanoj Gupta. Major tournaments over the next five years have been distributed solely among India, England, Australia, and New Zealand.

Under the newly released schedule, Australia and New Zealand will host the T20 World Cup in 2028. England, Ireland, and Scotland will jointly host the T20 showpiece in 2030, while England will also host the World Test Championship finals in 2029 and 2031. Meanwhile, India secured hosting rights for the 2029 Champions Trophy and will co-host the 2031 ODI World Cup alongside Bangladesh.

These allocations follow last year's Champions Trophy hosted by Pakistan, during which political friction caused India's matches and the tournament final to be shifted to Dubai. Consequently, the Pakistan Cricket Board agreed to a reciprocal arrangement with the BCCI ensuring that Pakistan’s matches in ICC events hosted by India over the next five years will occur at neutral venues. This dynamic likely influenced the decision to make Bangladesh a co-host for the 2031 ODI World Cup.

Strained political relations between India and Pakistan have frequently impacted matches on the pitch, raising concerns that political tensions could resurface if Pakistan qualifies for the 2029 Champions Trophy in India. Observers note that these recent tournament allocations highlight deep-seated governance issues within the sport as the cricket world navigates ongoing diplomatic divides.

stories.title: ICC Schedule Leaves Pakistan Without Tournament Hosting Rights Until 2031
stories.summary:
World cricket governance has come under scrutiny following the release of the International Cricket Council schedule for the 2028-2035 cycle, which excludes Pakistan from hosting any events until 2031. The ICC is chaired by Jay Shah, the former secretary of the Board of Control for Cricket in India who was re-elected unopposed, and is managed by chief executive officer Sanoj Gupta. The governing body split upcoming global tournaments entirely between India, England, Australia, and New Zealand.
