Federal Minister for Commerce Jam Kamal Khan and Turkmenistan’s Minister of Trade and Foreign Economic Relations, Dortguly Suleymanov, met in Islamabad on Monday to discuss methods for enhancing bilateral trade, regional connectivity, market access, and business cooperation. The meeting preceded the sixth session of the Pakistan–Turkmenistan Joint Intergovernmental Commission. Jam Kamal Khan emphasized developing practical partnerships in textiles, agriculture, food processing, manufacturing, and logistics, while noting that global freight disruptions make regional integration vital.

To improve connectivity, Jam Kamal Khan proposed direct flights and chartered cargo services between Islamabad and Ashgabat for time-sensitive agricultural exports. He also highlighted the expanding regional operations of Pakistan’s National Logistics Corporation and alternative trade routes for exports like Pakistani marble. Furthermore, he stressed the importance of business visa facilitation for investors and traders.

Turkmen Minister Dortguly Suleymanov addressed a recent decline in bilateral commerce, noting that trade turnover fell from over $36 million in 2025 down to roughly $15 million during the first nine months of 2026, primarily due to reduced textile exports. Both ministers agreed to nominate focal persons, such as Joint Secretary Maria for Pakistan, to coordinate trade-related matters. They also discussed updating exportable product lists, strengthening institutional ties, and boosting participation in international exhibitions.

Additionally, Jam Kamal Khan briefed his counterpart on Pakistan's five-year tariff rationalization program and the Ministry of Commerce's new online trade information portal. Both officials reaffirmed their commitment to achieving sustainable growth in economic relations through improved regional infrastructure and closer institutional coordination.

stories.title: State Bank of Pakistan Releases FY26 Report Highlighting Economic Resilience
stories.summary:
Pakistan’s central bank was compelled to raise its policy rate by 100 basis points in April after an energy shock driven by Middle East conflict pushed headline inflation into double digits, according to the State Bank of Pakistan's Governor’s Annual Report for FY26. Despite successive shocks including monsoon floods, trade tariff uncertainties, and geopolitical conflict, national economic indicators displayed resilience. Average national consumer price index inflation remained close to the upper bound of the medium-term target range, foreign exchange reserves surpassed targets, and real GDP recorded higher growth.

The report notes that average NCPI inflation was 5.5 percent from July to February 2026 before global oil price hikes pushed headline inflation into double digits from April onward. In response to the deteriorating inflation and external outlooks, the Monetary Policy Committee enacted the 100 basis point rate hike in April 2026 to contain secondary effects and maintain stability. Conversely, the SBP had reduced the rate by 50 basis points in December 2025 due to previously subdued inflation and stronger external accounts.

Regarding foreign exchange reserves, the SBP exceeded its target of $18 billion for the end of June 2026. The bank accomplished net foreign exchange purchases of $8.1 billion and reduced forward and swap liabilities by $1.6 billion, despite a moderate current account deficit. This reserve buildup, coupled with fiscal consolidation and successful International Monetary Fund reviews, improved sovereign ratings and exchange-rate stability.

The financial system maintained resilience as bank asset quality improved with a declining non-performing loan ratio, and capital adequacy ratios stayed well above regulatory requirements. Furthermore, the SBP pursued tertiary objectives by launching digital initiatives like the 'Zarkhez-e' agriculture lending platform, digital model villages, teen-accessible bank accounts, and the Pakistan Green Taxonomy.

stories.title: Autopsy Report Confirms Severe Torture of 13-Year-Old Domestic Worker
stories.summary:
The post-mortem report for 13-year-old domestic worker Fatima Asghar has confirmed she endured repeated and brutal physical torture before her death, sustaining at least 20 fresh and old injuries across her body. Released by the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences and handed over to the police, the autopsy details multiple wounds, bruises, scars, and signs of assault from her head to her feet. Investigators also observed severe swelling, blood clots in organs including the heart and kidneys, an old deteriorated wound on her left arm, and previous chest injuries.

Medical officers concluded that the cause of death was repeated physical assault resulting in severe inflammation, thromboembolism, and cardiopulmonary arrest. Preliminary investigations indicate the minor may have been subjected to abuse for approximately three years. The findings have also sparked questions regarding whether other individuals linked to the case were aware of the mistreatment.

Fatima was employed at the official residence of a senior Federal Investigation Agency officer stationed at the Police Lines Headquarters in Islamabad’s H-11 area. Legal experts have urged authorities to examine the roles of the FIA officer and the victim's father, while arguing that Section 328-A of the Pakistan Penal Code concerning cruelty to a child should be applied. Earlier on Monday, an Islamabad court granted a four-day physical remand for the two main suspects in the case: the senior FIA officer's wife and a religious cleric.

stories.title: Bangladesh Garment Workers Clash With Police Amid Nationwide Wage Protests
stories.summary:
Bangladeshi police deployed tear gas and stun grenades on Tuesday to disperse thousands of garment workers protesting the postponement of a key wage board meeting in Gazipur, near Dhaka. Demonstrators retaliated by hurling bricks, setting vehicles on fire, and blocking the major highway connecting Dhaka and Mymensingh. The unrest highlights growing worker frustration in South Asia's prominent garment export hub, which generates $38 billion annually and employs over four million people across 4,500 factories.

Workers are demanding a 140 percent increase in their minimum monthly wage, seeking 30,000 taka ($240) up from the current 12,500 taka, to cope with surging costs for food, housing, transport, and healthcare. Tensions have been further exacerbated because roughly 500 factories are currently shut down, prompting owners to invoke 'no work, no pay' labour laws that withhold wages during production halts. Protests also spread to other industrial hubs like Savar and Ashulia.

The government-established wage board, which includes employer and worker representatives, was originally scheduled to meet on Monday but postponed after a workers' representative fell ill. The next negotiation session is set for November 23, with a finalized minimum wage expected in December to take effect in January. In response to Tuesday's violence, the Border Guard Bangladesh intensified patrols across industrial zones using drones and body-worn cameras to monitor the situation, as the sector faces intense pressure during the peak Christmas export period.

stories.title: Pakistan Defeats India to Reach Blind Asia Cup Cricket Final
stories.summary:
Pakistan secured a dramatic one-wicket victory over defending champions India on Tuesday to qualify for the final of the Asia Cup Blind Cricket Tournament in Dhaka. Chasing a target of 180 runs at the Anwar Cricket Stadium in Bashundhara, Pakistan successfully reached 180-9 in their allotted 20 overs.

India had won the toss and elected to bat first, posting a total of 179-6. Their innings was anchored by captain Durgarao, who scored 62 runs, with additional contributions from Sanjay Kumar with 30 runs and D. Venkatesh with 26 runs. Babar Ali, Badar Munir, and Muhammad Idrees each claimed one wicket for the bowling side.

In response, Pakistan's chase was led by captain Nisar Ali, who contributed 64 runs off 51 deliveries, while teammate Muhammad Safdar added 31 runs. The match came down to a tense finish when Pakistan required seven runs from the final two deliveries of the innings. All-rounder Niamatullah performed under pressure by hitting a six and a four off the last two balls to seal the win.

Nisar Ali earned the player of the match award but dedicated the honour to Niamatullah for his decisive final-over performance. Pakistan advanced to the tournament final scheduled for November 20, where they will face the winner of the upcoming match between India and Bangladesh.

stories.title: Election Commission of Punjab Approves Two-Phase Local Government Polls
stories.summary:
The Election Commission of Pakistan officially approved conducting local government elections across Punjab in two distinct phases, with the initial phase set for February 7, 2027. The electoral body issued a letter to the Punjab chief secretary agreeing to the provincial government's request to split the voting across 18 district groups per phase.

The first phase will encompass Lahore, while Faisalabad and Multan are designated for the subsequent phase. The February date was selected after provincial authorities requested a timeline within January or February due to favourable weather conditions. Initially, the province planned elections between December 2026 and January 2027, but a cabinet committee subsequently recommended a postponement to April 2027 to avoid smog, dense fog, Ramazan, and the unavailability of schoolteachers.

Political stakeholders have begun preparing for the electoral exercise despite prior reservations. Pakistan People's Party Women's Wing President Faryal Talpur urged party workers in Lahore to ready themselves for the local polls, and Punjab Governor Sardar Saleem Haider Khan confirmed his party's participation. Jamaat-e-Islami Deputy Emir Liaquat Baloch stated his party would also contest the elections.

Additionally, the Election Commission stated its readiness to conduct local government elections in Islamabad, confirming that arrangements for printing the required ballot papers have already been finalized.

stories.title: Rawalpindi Police Miss Statutory Deadline to Submit Hina Javed Murder Challan
stories.summary:
Authorities in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, have missed the legal deadline to present the investigation report regarding the violent death of Hina Javed. The victim was discovered under suspicious conditions inside her apartment's bathroom situated in the Lal Kurti neighborhood on August 20, 2026. While regulations mandate that law enforcement file the challan within a two-week period, a span of 86 days has elapsed without the necessary paperwork reaching the court.

In response to the inaction, the District Prosecution Branch issued formal correspondence to top law enforcement officials, including the Rawalpindi City Police Officer, the Senior Superintendent of Police, and the Station House Officer of the Civil Lines Police Station. The directive urges immediate steps to finalize and present the case documents to the judicial authorities without further delay, as growing scrutiny surrounds the stalled legal proceedings.

Investigators have zeroed in on a domestic worker named Zeeshan, who stayed in the residence's servant quarters, designating him as the main suspect in the homicide. Additionally, the victim's spouse, Faisal Asghar, who resided with his father on an upper level of the building, is also implicated. Both Zeeshan and Faisal Asghar are presently being held in judicial custody while the inquiry continues.

The handling of the matter has drawn sharp criticism from the victim's relatives, who have repeatedly voiced their frustration regarding the direction and management of the probe. Meanwhile, parents of the domestic employee have maintained that their son holds no responsibility for the crime, keeping public interest high as the prosecution seeks to push the judicial process forward.

stories.title: British Royals Arrive in Mumbai by E-Rickshaw for Earthshot Prize
stories.summary:
Prince William and Kate Middleton arrived in Mumbai on Tuesday via an electric auto-rickshaw driven by the prince, heading toward a waterfront location overlooking the Bandra-Worli Sea Link bridge. The royal couple are undertaking a three-day journey across the nation centered on the Earthshot Prize, an environmental initiative designed to discover and expand ecological solutions. The program grants five victors an award of £1 million, equivalent to $1.3 million, to help grow their projects.

During their stop, the pair greeted and posed for photographs with the local finalists of the competition, later sharing the image on their social media accounts alongside a statement highlighting India's strong representation among the prize's honorees and contenders. Their itinerary includes a scheduled journey to New Delhi on Wednesday to hold discussions with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, marking the conclusion of their current tour.

The excursion represents a major milestone for the Princess of Wales, serving as her most prominent international journey since undergoing medical care for cancer in 2024. Following preventative chemotherapy for an unspecified type of the disease, the 44-year-old royal scaled back her official responsibilities for a period. Although she has slowly resumed public duties since entering remission, she has largely remained in the United Kingdom, with a brief solo trip to Italy in May marking her only other major overseas engagement since 2024.

stories.title: Israeli and Pakistani Ambassadors Meet in Rare Diplomatic Encounter at UN
stories.summary:
In an unusual diplomatic interaction, Israeli Ambassador Jonathan Peled met with Pakistan's ambassador to the United Nations, Tahir Hussain Andrabi, in Geneva. During the encounter, the Israeli envoy officially presented his credentials to his Pakistani counterpart at the international body's location in Switzerland.

The meeting stands out because the two nations do not maintain formal diplomatic relations with each other. The interaction took place under the framework of United Nations proceedings in Geneva, bringing representatives from the two countries into direct contact despite the absence of official bilateral ties.

Photographic evidence of the event was shared publicly by the Israeli envoy through a post on the social media platform X. The image captured the moment the credentials were formally presented between the diplomatic representatives.

While the encounter does not signal a broader shift in geopolitical relations between the two governments, it highlights the unique diplomatic dynamics that occasionally occur within multilateral organizations like the United Nations.

stories.title: Asian Development Bank Approves $500 Million Loan for Pakistan Pension Reforms
stories.summary:
The Asian Development Bank has approved a $500 million results-based loan designed to assist Pakistan in reforming its federal civil pension system. Announced by the Manila-based lending agency, the initiative aims to contain escalating pension-related fiscal pressures, enhance the sustainability of the system, and create fiscal space for necessary development and social spending.

Pakistan's federal pension expenditures have expanded nearly fivefold since the 2016 fiscal year, currently exceeding Rs1 trillion annually. The existing unfunded and noncontributory legacy defined benefit scheme relies completely on annual budget allocations, which generates growing fiscal pressure over time. ADB Country Director for Pakistan Emma Fan noted that the program will sustain and institutionalize important steps already taken by the country to strengthen its federal pension administration, boost financial transparency through digital systems, and improve service delivery.

The new funding will directly support the initial phase of the government's Pension Reform Implementation Plan. This includes facilitating the transition to a defined contribution pension scheme mandatory for federal civil employees appointed starting in July 2024. In August, the government formalized agreements with 16 pension fund managers to operationalize the Defined Contribution Pension Fund Scheme.

ADB senior economist Aiko Kikkawa previously highlighted that Pakistan's pension framework suffered from low contribution rates and weak systems, making it unsustainable over the long run. Most government positions previously relied on unfunded pensions financed entirely through tax revenues. The current ADB financing aims to resolve these vulnerabilities by building stronger institutions and promoting a transparent, sustainable pension system for beneficiaries.

stories.title: راولپنڈی ٹیسٹ: پاکستان نے سری لنکا کو پہلی اننگز میں 98 رنز پر آؤٹ کر دیا
stories.summary:
راولپنڈی میں کھیلے جانے والے دوسرے ٹیسٹ میچ کے پہلے روز پاکستان نے شاندار بولنگ کا مظاہرہ کرتے ہوئے سری لنکا کی پوری ٹیم کو پہلی اننگز میں محض 98 رنز پر آؤٹ کر دیا۔ منگل کے روز پاکستانی کپتان بابر اعظم نے ٹاس جیت کر پہلے بولنگ کا فیصلہ کیا جو کہ فاسٹ بولرز نے درست ثابت کر دیا۔

سری لنکا کی پہلی وکٹ چھ رنز پر گری جب ثاقب خان نے پسندو سوریا بندارا کو آؤٹ کیا۔ مہمان ٹیم کی وکٹیں وقفے وقفے سے گرتی رہیں اور کھانے کے وقفے تک چھ کھلاڑی آؤٹ ہو چکے تھے۔ کھانے کے بعد سری لنکا کی ٹیم صرف ساڑھے چھ اوورز کھیل سکی اور پوری ٹیم 98 رنز پر ڈھیر ہو گئی۔

پاکستان کی جانب سے محمد عباس نے 14 رنز دے کر تین، رضااللہ نے 21 رنز کے عوض تین اور عامر جمال نے 24 رنز دے کر تین وکٹیں حاصل کیں۔ اس کے علاوہ ثاقب خان نے بھی ایک کھلاڑی کو آؤٹ کیا۔ کرکٹ تجزیہ کاروں اور سوشل میڈیا صارفین نے راولپنڈی کے اس گراؤنڈ پر کسی بھی ٹیم کا اب تک کا یہ سب سے کم سکور قرار دیا ہے اور پاکستانی پیسرز کی کارفرماجی کی تعریف کی ہے۔

اس میچ میں پاکستان کی طرف سے بابر اعظم، اذان اویس، طیب عارف، محمد طٰہ، سعود شکیل، سلمان علی آغا، غازی غوری، محمد عباس، رضااللہ، ثاقب خان اور عامر جمال میدان میں اترے۔ جبکہ سری لنکا کی ٹیم میں کشال مینڈس، لاہیرو ادارا، پسندو سوریا بندارا، دنیش چندی مل، کامندو مینڈس، دھننجایا ڈی سلوا، سونال دنوشا، میلان رتھنائیکا، پربھات جے سوریا، لاہیرو کمارا اور اسیتھا فرنینڈو شامل تھے۔

stories.title: Sri Lanka Records Lowest Test Innings Total at Rawalpindi Stadium
stories.summary:
Sri Lanka suffered a severe batting collapse, getting bowled out for 98 against Pakistan on Tuesday during the second Test match at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. Opting to bowl first after winning the toss, Pakistan's pace attack exploited the conditions effectively to dismiss the visiting team after lunch.

The visitors' total of 98 established a new, unwanted record as the lowest-ever innings score recorded at the Rawalpindi venue. This performance surpassed England's previous low of 112, which occurred during the third innings of the first Test against Pakistan in October 2024. Sri Lanka also became the first team to be dismissed for fewer than 100 runs in a Test innings at this specific ground.

Other notable low totals at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium include Pakistan's 138 against South Africa in October 2025 and the West Indies' 139 against Pakistan in November 1997. Further down the list are Pakistan's 145 against Australia in 1998, Pakistan's 146 against Bangladesh in August 2024, Bangladesh's 168 in February 2020, and New Zealand's 168 in November 1996.

During Sri Lanka's historic collapse, captain Kusal Mendis provided the primary resistance by scoring 32 runs from 50 balls, including five boundaries. However, the rest of the batting order failed to manage Pakistan's bowling attack, resulting in a disastrous opening outing in the series-deciding fixture.

stories.title: Saudi Energy Firm Delta Studies $30 Billion Pakistan Pipeline Plan
stories.summary:
Saudi Arabian energy company Delta Energy Saudi has signed an agreement with Inter State Gas Systems to explore a massive $30 billion energy infrastructure development in Pakistan. Announced on Tuesday, the proposed programme will evaluate a natural gas pipeline entering Pakistan through its western border and extending toward Gwadar, alongside potential extensions to the eastern border, liquefied natural gas facilities, and processing and storage terminals. 

The initiative also envisions constructing a pipeline from Chaman on the Afghan border across Pakistan toward the Indian border near Fazilka, which Delta Energy considers a core strategic commitment requiring formal agreements with authorities in both nations. The scheme identifies resources from Afghanistan, such as the Kashk gas concession, as potential supplies and operates separately from the Turkmenistan-Afghanistan-Pakistan-India project. 

Under a revised project structure mentioned in the report, Pakistan would hold a 74 percent share while Russia would hold 26 percent, with Pakistan providing the majority of the financing. Officials noted that prior pipeline initiatives intended to bring gas into Pakistan have experienced years of delays.

The signed agreement strictly establishes a framework for evaluating the projects rather than acting as a final investment decision or a binding financial commitment. The exploratory efforts matter as a potential step toward addressing regional energy needs, though all routes and infrastructure remain subject to future formal approvals and agreements.

stories.title: Pakistan Pacing Attack Bundles Out Sri Lanka for 98 in Test
stories.summary:
Pakistan's pace attack dismantled Sri Lanka for 98 runs on the opening day of the series-deciding second Test match in Rawalpindi on Tuesday. Sent in to bat first by Pakistan captain Babar Azam on a green-top pitch, the touring side was bowled out in 35.3 overs.

Pakistan made a strategic change to their lineup, bringing in pace-bowling all-rounder Aamir Jamal to replace spin all-rounder Arafat Minhas. Saqib Khan, who claimed seven wickets on his debut during the series opener, delivered an early breakthrough by removing Pasindu Sooriyabandara for two runs in the fourth over. Veteran fast bowler Mohammad Abbas then dismissed Dinesh Chandimal for seven and Kamindu Mendis for eight, leaving the visitors struggling at 25-3.

Razaullah deepened Sri Lanka's troubles by taking two quick wickets, sending back Lahiru Udara for four and first-Test centurion Dhananjaya de Silva for one, reducing the team to 36-5. Skipper Kusal Mendis and Sonal Dinusha managed to orchestrate a brief recovery through a 49-run partnership for the sixth wicket. Just before the interval, Aamir Jamal broke this partnership by dismissing Kusal Mendis for 32 runs.

Only two Sri Lankan batters managed to reach double figures during the innings: captain Kusal Mendis with 32 and Sonal Dinusha with 21. The bowling honors for Pakistan were shared among Mohammad Abbas, Razaullah, and Aamir Jamal, who claimed three wickets each to rout the visitors quickly on the first day.

stories.title: Sindh Government Launches Portal for Online Domicile and PRC Issuance
stories.summary:
The Sindh government has officially launched a new e-domicile and Permanent Residence Certificate (PRC) portal, allowing residents to apply for and obtain these official documents directly from their homes. Sindh Chief Secretary Asif Haider Shah inaugurated the digital system, which is designed to eliminate the long queues previously common at government offices.

Speaking at the launch ceremony, the chief secretary explained that citizens can now submit applications using a dedicated mobile application without needing to visit physical offices. The digital platform substantially reduces processing times, turning a procedure that historically took an entire week into one that can now be finished in a matter of hours.

Chief Secretary Asif Haider Shah noted that acquiring a domicile certificate is frequently a young person's initial interaction with government administrative systems. Streamlining this procedure is intended to enhance the general public perception of government service delivery. Furthermore, the E-Domicile system incorporates digital verification features to prevent fraudulent applications and the submission of fake paperwork.

Authorities plan to expand this digital facility progressively to other districts across the province to guarantee widespread public access. The initiative marks a significant step toward modernizing regional administrative services and improving convenience for residents throughout Sindh.

stories.title: Jamaat-e-Islami Chief Supports Smaller Administrative Units with Broad Consensus
stories.summary:
Jamaat-e-Islami chief Hafiz Naeem ur Rehman expressed support for smaller administrative units during a media talk in Lahore on Tuesday. He noted that such divisions should be implemented if they improve national governance, but emphasized that major decisions require broad consensus. According to the party leader, a referendum should be conducted if it follows constitutional procedures.

During his address, the Jamaat-e-Islami leader criticized provincial governments for avoiding local council elections. He pointed out that even when authorities do conduct polls, they fail to devolve powers down to the lower levels.

Why this matters is that the debate over administrative decentralization and local government powers directly impacts provincial governance and public representation across the country. Such structural policies shape how administrative responsibilities and local resources are distributed among citizens.

Background details from the briefing include the organization's ongoing stance regarding administrative reforms and local democracy. The remarks highlight persistent political tensions surrounding local government authority and the implementation of structural changes.

stories.title: Iran and Oman Foreign Ministers Discuss Shipping Security Amid Hormuz Blockade
stories.summary:
The foreign ministers of Iran and Oman met in Muscat on Tuesday to discuss diplomatic options aimed at containing regional tensions and safeguarding shipping routes. Iranian top diplomat Abbas Araghchi and Omani counterpart Badr Albusaidi held talks focused on revitalizing channels of dialogue and negotiation, as reported by the Oman News Agency.

The discussions aimed to broaden mutual understanding among involved parties and prevent the ongoing crisis from expanding further. Both officials emphasized the critical need to secure maritime passages and maintain uninterrupted international navigation and trade through the Strait of Hormuz.

This diplomatic engagement matters because Tehran has maintained a blockade of the vital Strait of Hormuz for months, sparked by the Middle East war that began with United States and Israel strikes on February 28. Regular Iranian attacks on vessels plying the main exit route for Gulf energy exports have forced ships to use routes authorized by Iran, while soaring oil prices have increased fuel and consumer costs globally.

Key details involve the ongoing maritime restrictions and the persistent economic fallout affecting businesses and consumers worldwide. The talks represent a concerted effort by regional diplomats to address the blockade and explore diplomatic paths to ease the strained situation.

stories.title: Pakistan Pace Attack Dismisses Sri Lanka for 98 on Day One in Rawalpindi
stories.summary:
Pakistan's pace attack swiftly dismantled Sri Lanka for a total of 98 runs on the opening day of the second and series-deciding Test match in Rawalpindi on Tuesday. Sent in to bat by Pakistan on a green-top pitch, the visiting team was bowled out in just 35.3 overs.

The host team's bowling performance was led by Mohammad Abbas, Razaullah, and Aamer Jamal, who each claimed three wickets. Abbas finished with figures of 3-14, Razaullah recorded 3-21, and Jamal secured 3-24.

For Sri Lanka, skipper Kusal Mendis scored 32 runs and Sonal Dinusha added 21 runs. They were the only two visiting batters to reach double figures during the difficult innings.

This collapse is significant for the outcome of the series-deciding Test match, putting Pakistan in a commanding position early in the game. Background context highlights that the match follows a previous Test between the two sides.

stories.title: Gold and Silver Prices Remain Steady Across Pakistan on Tuesday
stories.summary:
Gold prices in Pakistan held steady on Tuesday, mirroring stable trends observed in the international market. The local market rates for the precious metal showed no movement throughout the day, according to figures released by the All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association.

Specifically, the price of gold per tola remained at Rs408,936. Similarly, the price for 10 grams of gold stayed unchanged at Rs350,596. This stability follows a decline of Rs2,000 on Monday, which had brought the per tola price to Rs408,936.

In the global market, the international rate of gold also remained flat at $3,864 per ounce. Meanwhile, local silver prices mirrored the broader market stability, holding firm at Rs5,228 per tola without any price fluctuations.

This steady pricing matters to local consumers, investors, and businesses tracking precious metals for financial planning and jewelry retail. The lack of movement provides a temporary pause following recent market adjustments.

stories.title: Pakistan Bowlers Dismiss Sri Lanka for 98 in Rawalpindi Test
stories.summary:
Pakistan's bowling attack put on a dominant display on Tuesday, dismissing Sri Lanka for just 98 runs in 35.3 overs on the opening day of the second Test at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. Opting to field first after winning the toss, Pakistan exploited favorable movement to leave the visiting team struggling at 36-5 by lunch before wrapping up the innings shortly after the interval, taking the final four wickets for only 13 runs.

Mohammad Abbas, Razaullah, and Aamer Jamal spearheaded the attack by claiming three wickets each, while Saqib Khan contributed one dismissal. Abbas delivered an economical spell of 3-14 across 14 overs with six maidens. Razaullah returned figures of 3-21 in eight overs, and Jamal took 3-24 in 5.3 overs. Saqib made the initial breakthrough by removing Pasindu Sooriyabandara early in the innings.

Sri Lanka's resistance was anchored by a 49-run sixth-wicket partnership between captain Kusal Mendis and Sonal Dinusha. Kusal top-scored with 32 runs from 50 balls, hitting five boundaries, while Dinusha contributed 21 runs from 40 deliveries. Aside from this partnership, the visiting batting lineup failed to establish momentum against the disciplined bowling attack.

This total marks the lowest innings score recorded at the Rawalpindi venue, eclipsing England's previous low of 112 set in 2024. The performance places Pakistan in a strong position as they seek to build a decisive advantage in the ongoing Test series against Sri Lanka.

stories.title: Fire Erupts at Rashidabad Factory Following Suspected Boiler Explosion
stories.summary:
A major fire broke out on the ground floor of a factory in Rashidabad, Baldia Town, Karachi, on Tuesday following a reported boiler explosion. The facility accommodates both a garments factory and a food manufacturing unit, triggering immediate concerns that the flames might spread to adjacent sections of the multi-use industrial premises.

Emergency services launched a large-scale response, deploying eight fire engines and a snorkel vehicle to combat the blaze. Police and local administration officials, including Keamari SSP Singhar Malik and Deputy Commissioner Sattar Hakro, rushed to the location to supervise rescue operations. Law enforcement personnel cordoned off the surrounding area to ensure public safety and maintain a clear path for emergency vehicles.

Authorities confirmed that no casualties had been recorded as firefighting efforts continued. However, complications arose after oil reportedly leaked from a storage tank, creating the risk of a secondary incident. Firefighters worked to secure the area and prevent the flames from reaching nearby industrial buildings.

Providing a progress update, SSP Singhar Malik announced that roughly 60 percent of the fire had been successfully contained. Emergency crews managed to stop the blaze from spreading to neighboring factories, while cooling and containment operations remained ongoing at the scene.

stories.title: Asian Development Bank Approves $500 Million Loan for Pension Reforms in Pakistan
stories.summary:
The Asian Development Bank (ADB) has endorsed a $500 million results-based loan designed to assist Pakistan in reforming its federal civil pension system. Announced on Tuesday, the financing aims to alleviate escalating pension-related fiscal pressures, enhance the long-term sustainability of the system, and free up public funds for vital development and social initiatives.

Expenditures on federal pensions in Pakistan have expanded nearly fivefold since the 2016 fiscal year, surpassing PRs1 trillion annually. The traditional unfunded and noncontributory legacy defined benefit scheme relies exclusively on annual budget allocations, creating severe financial strain as obligations continue to grow. ADB Country Director for Pakistan Emma Fan noted that the program will institutionalize the steps Pakistan has already initiated to strengthen its federal framework.

The funds will directly support the initial phase of the Pakistani government's Pension Reform Implementation Plan. This includes facilitating the transition toward a defined contribution pension scheme, which is mandatory for federal civil employees appointed starting in July 2024. The ADB stated the initiative will also focus on upgrading pension management to minimize liabilities and boosting financial transparency through digital infrastructure.

Additionally, the program seeks to improve pension service delivery and elevate financial literacy among program beneficiaries. By strengthening institutional processes, the ADB-backed reforms intend to achieve lasting economic stability within the country's public expenditure framework.

stories.title: Supernet Technologies Targets Growth Through Services, Cybersecurity, and Regional Expansion
stories.summary:
Supernet Technologies Limited (STL) is pursuing business growth by focusing on higher-margin services, cybersecurity, and international markets. The strategic pivot follows the consolidation of its operating business into a single listed entity and the successful raising of Rs915 million through a rights issue.

During a recent corporate briefing, company representatives reported that services accounted for roughly 76% of their Rs8.08 billion revenue in the 2026 fiscal year, up from approximately 46% the previous year. Service revenue climbed to Rs6.16 billion from Rs4.23 billion, lifting the gross margin to 24% from 19.8% despite lower overall sales. Out of the rights issue proceeds, Rs465 million was allocated to working capital for a Rs1 billion critical-communications project slated for FY2027 delivery, while Rs450 million went toward settling acquisition considerations owed to Telecard.

Cybersecurity operations are also driving profitability through SuperSecure, an enterprise in which STL maintains an 80% stake. SuperSecure generated Rs1.4 billion in FY2026 revenue, yielding a gross profit of Rs313 million and a profit after tax of Rs170 million. Management highlighted an active pipeline of critical infrastructure projects exceeding Rs1亿元 alongside advanced-stage opportunities anticipated to close by December 2026.

Internationally, STL is establishing a commercial hub in the United Arab Emirates under the Supernet Global platform and deploying satellite connectivity across Africa. Looking toward FY2027, the company aims to expand recurring managed services, cross-sell cybersecurity products, and improve collections, while remaining mindful of pricing pressures, foreign exchange fluctuations, and macroeconomic risks.

stories.title: Pakistan Information Minister Defends Public Debate on New Administrative Provinces
stories.summary:
Information Minister Attaullah Tarar responded on Tuesday to statements made by Pakistan Peoples Party Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari, criticizing what he termed "double standards" within political leadership. Bilawal had previously called for a political reset, arguing that the country's institutional system was deliberately dismantled rather than collapsing on its own. Tarar countered that political parties have participated in the existing system for decades and cannot distance themselves from its shortcomings.

Addressing the ongoing discourse regarding the creation of new provinces, Tarar asserted that the debate cannot and should not be stopped, calling it a constitutional and democratic requirement. The dialogue originally gained traction in July when Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi proposed additional administrative units to improve governance and deliver justice. While parties like the Muttahida Qaumi Movement-Pakistan supported the concept, it faced intense resistance in Sindh, culminating in a unanimous provincial assembly resolution rejecting any division of the region.

Tarar emphasized that referendums are a legitimate constitutional path and that the public must be allowed to decide whether they want smaller administrative units. He criticized politicians for attempting to use politics as an excuse to avoid accountability and questioned critiques directed at the National Accountability Bureau, noting that the agency's reforms were originally introduced by the very leaders currently blaming it for systemic failures.

The debate highlights deep political divisions within Pakistan's ruling coalition and provincial governments regarding administrative devolution and governance reforms. Tarar maintained that the will of the people must be respected and that discussions surrounding governance and public services should continue transparently both inside and outside parliament.

stories.title: US Government Confirms Investigation Into Singapore Firm Megaspeed Over Chip Exports
stories.summary:
The United States government officially confirmed that it is investigating Megaspeed, a data center firm based in Singapore, over suspected chip exports designed to bypass US regulations and deliver Nvidia's advanced technology to China. This probe came to light following a major tech scandal involving Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who stepped down from his position last week after disclosing multiple extramarital affairs, including one with Alice Huang, a former Chinese executive at Megaspeed whom US authorities suspect of spying for Beijing.

In a joint statement, the US Commerce and Justice departments announced their collaboration to enforce the law against Megaspeed for any potential criminal activities. The Commerce Department initiated an inquiry into Megaspeed for export control violations back in 2024. Subsequently, authorities requested sales records from Nvidia in May 2025 regarding direct or indirect transactions with Megaspeed. By the following month, Nvidia added Megaspeed to its no-sell list, while federal agents conducted an in-person audit at the Singapore company and interviewed Alice Huang.

The enforcement action eventually transitioned into a criminal investigation led by the Department of Justice. Meanwhile, the controversy has triggered political friction within US President Donald Trump's administration. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent criticized the commerce department for allegedly overlooking warnings that Megaspeed was funneling Nvidia technology to China, prompting Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to agree to a congressional testimony before the Senate.

Jensen Huang, who led Nvidia since its establishment in 1993, has also agreed to testify behind closed doors before the House of Representatives ahead of Thanksgiving on November 26. The unfolding situation highlights intense ongoing tech competition between the United States and China, leading Washington to implement stricter export control measures on artificial intelligence silicon chips following the scandal.

stories.title: US and Singapore Detail Investigation Into Cloud Firm Megaspeed
stories.summary:
The United States Commerce Department and Justice Department disclosed that an investigation into Singapore-based cloud-computing firm Megaspeed began two years ago. Megaspeed, an Asia-Pacific partner of Nvidia, faced intense scrutiny after former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang experienced a scandal involving former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang.

According to joint statements, US trade authorities flagged suspicious activities regarding sensitive semiconductor diversions in 2024. By mid-2025, investigators requested records from Nvidia, leading to Megaspeed being placed on a restricted sales list. US agents and Singaporean law enforcement subsequently conducted an on-site inspection and interviewed Alice Huang, who left her position as CEO in August 2025.

While Singaporean authorities found insufficient evidence to charge her with false declarations regarding server purchases, she received a warning for providing inaccurate information and was barred from re-entering the city-state. Meanwhile, US intelligence agencies are examining potential ties between Alice Huang and Chinese intelligence, though Beijing has strongly denied these allegations.

The public disclosure underscores the heightened international focus on semiconductor supply chains and export controls involving major technology firms. As investigations involving Megaspeed and related individuals continue, Singapore has agreed to maintain ongoing discussions with Washington regarding the matter.

stories.title: Pakistani and Iranian Officials Confer on Regional Security Issues
stories.summary:
Field Marshal Asim Munir, Pakistan's Chief of Defence Forces and Army Staff, met with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Rawalpindi to review regional security dynamics and collaborative measures. The discussions centered on strengthening mutual trust and addressing shared security challenges between the neighboring countries.

Foreign Minister Araghchi lauded Pakistan's ongoing efforts to foster regional peace and voiced a strong desire to expand bilateral cooperation. The meeting followed Araghchi's participation in the Economic Cooperation Organisation ministerial gathering in Islamabad, where he highlighted the necessity of reliable energy frameworks and regional stability amid ongoing geopolitical conflicts.

Pakistan has actively participated in diplomatic mediation between Iran and the United States, having previously brokered a temporary ceasefire and hosted direct talks earlier in the year. Although hostilities have intermittently resumed, Pakistani military and civilian leaders have maintained regular high-level visits to Tehran to support long-term peace initiatives.

These sustained diplomatic efforts remain crucial for preventing further escalation in West Asia. Through continued dialogue and strategic partnerships, both nations aim to protect regional infrastructure and encourage peaceful resolutions to ongoing disputes.

stories.title: Panther Tyres Expands Renewable Capacity With New Solar Plant
stories.summary:
Panther Tyres Limited has successfully commissioned a new 3.5-megawatt solar power plant at its manufacturing facility, boosting the company's total captive solar generation capacity to 6 megawatts. The company officially reported this expansion through a notice filed with the Pakistan Stock Exchange on Tuesday.

The latest renewable energy project integrates high-efficiency Jinko 720W solar panels paired with Huawei inverters. This green initiative aligns with the manufacturer's Environmental, Social, and Governance objectives, designed to curb carbon emissions by approximately 4,700 metric tons annually while improving operational cost efficiency.

Originally established as a private company in 1983 and later converted into a public limited enterprise in 2003, Panther Tyres specializes in producing vehicle tyres and tubes. The firm previously installed a 2.5-megawatt solar system last year as part of its broader transition toward alternative energy sources.

Amid shifting commercial energy landscapes in Pakistan, Panther Tyres continues to implement strategic cost-cutting and market diversification measures. These steps include redeeming financial instruments like Sukuk certificates and exploring new geographical markets to ensure stable, long-term business growth.

stories.title: New Zealand All-Rounder Mitchell Santner Ruled Out of India Tests
stories.summary:
New Zealand all-rounder and limited-overs captain Mitchell Santner will miss the upcoming two-Test series against India after suffering a fracture in his non-bowling right hand. The injury occurred when he was struck by the ball while batting during Sunday's fifth One-day International against India. Scans confirmed the broken bone, leaving his participation in the subsequent four-Test series in Australia, starting December 9 in Perth, uncertain.

New Zealand Cricket stated that his return-to-play timeline is currently being evaluated, with updates on his status for the Australian matches to follow. The Test series against India begins on Thursday in Wellington and concludes with a second match in Christchurch on November 27. These fixtures mark the first red-ball meeting between the two nations since New Zealand's 3-0 series victory in India in 2024.

To fill the vacancy in the 14-man squad, selectors have called up spin-bowling all-rounder Dean Foxcroft, who made his Test debut against Ireland in May. Given that New Zealand pitches typically favor seam bowling, captain Tom Latham might utilize part-time spin options like Glenn Phillips and Rachin Ravindra to support a four-man pace attack.

stories.title: IRC and SECP Partner to Boost Women's Financial Inclusion in Pakistan
stories.summary:
International Rescue Committee President and Chief Executive Officer David Miliband announced that his organization will partner with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan to expand women's financial inclusion and support women entrepreneurs. Speaking as the chief keynote guest at an SECP seminar on financial literacy and inclusion, the former UK Foreign Secretary emphasized that combining economic opportunities with financial education is vital for sustainable independence.

During the event, SECP Chairman Dr Kabir Ahmed Sidhu noted that limited financial literacy remains a significant obstacle to public participation in the capital market. He outlined ongoing initiatives to facilitate micro-loans for women and help youth make sound financial choices, with a goal of raising stock market investors to 2.5 million through the Capital Market Development Fund.

Official briefings revealed that women account for 81.9 percent of active borrowers from non-bank microfinance institutions, which disbursed Rs236.2 billion to female borrowers in fiscal year 2026. Additionally, recent educational outreach efforts reached 1,500 teachers and 2,000 students across Gilgit-Baltistan, as officials discussed future collaborative initiatives to deliver financial education to women, youth, and crisis-affected populations.

stories.title: Pakistan Pace Attack Leaves Sri Lanka Struggling at Lunch on Day One
stories.summary:
Pakistan's seamers dismantled Sri Lanka's top order, reducing the visitors to 85-6 by lunch on the opening day of the second Test at Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium. After winning the toss and choosing to field on a green pitch, the hosts quickly capitalized on favorable bowling conditions to leave Sri Lanka reeling at 36-5 before a brief recovery.

Opening bowler Mohammad Abbas and fast bowler Razaullah spearheaded the attack with two wickets each, while Saqib Khan and Aamer Jamal chipped in with one dismissal apiece. Abbas maintained immense pressure with an economical spell of two wickets and just 12 runs from 11 overs, while Razaullah clocked speeds up to 146 kilometers per hour. Sri Lanka's early struggles saw experienced batters like Dinesh Chandimal and Dhananjaya de Silva depart cheaply.

Captain Kusal Mendis attempted a counterattack, compiling 32 runs from 50 deliveries and sharing a 49-run sixth-wicket partnership with Sonal Dinusha. Aamer broke the stand by removing Kusal just before the interval, leaving Dinusha unbeaten on 15 alongside Milan Rathnayaka as the team reached 85-6 in 29 overs.

stories.title: Ten-Year-Old Mustafa Sheharyar Wins Three Silver Medals at National Swimming
stories.summary:
Ten-year-old swimmer Mustafa Sheharyar Rana secured three silver medals representing Punjab at the National Age-Group Swimming Championship. The tournament took place at the KMC Sports Complex in Karachi, running from November 13 to 15, and gathered young swimming competitors from across the nation.

Competing within the Under-10 age category, Mustafa earned an individual silver medal in the 50-meter backstroke event. He further contributed to his medal count by joining teammates Abdul Rafay, Omer Hassan, and Zain Razaque as part of the Punjab squads that finished second in both the 4x100m freestyle relay and the 4x50m medley relay.

These podium finishes highlight the discipline and consistent training of the young athlete at an early age. Mustafa previously demonstrated his potential by earning recognition as the fastest Under-10 swimmer at the Chief Minister Punjab Age Group Inter-School Swimming Championship.

The latest achievements cement his reputation as an emerging swimming talent from Punjab, showcasing his ability to compete successfully at the national level alongside peers from various regions.

stories.title: Vinicius Scores Hat-Trick to Lead Brazil in Seven-Goal Victory Over Singapore
stories.summary:
Forward Vinicius Jr scored a rapid hat-trick to help Brazil secure a commanding 7-0 victory in an international friendly against Singapore on Tuesday. The emphatic win served as a strong response for the five-time world champions following a surprising 3-2 defeat against Japan.

Vinicius completed his three goals within a 21-minute span during the match. The dominant performance also featured goals from his Real Madrid teammate Endrick, along with Estevao Willian and Rayan, while Singapore right-back Raoul Suhaimi contributed an own goal to compound the hosts' deficit.

The 26-year-old forward had recently discussed his slower start to the season with Real Madrid, noting that a reduced training schedule and ongoing transfer interest may have impacted his form after signing a long-term contract extension in August. Prior to the Singapore rout, he had scored two goals in the previous match against Japan.

The friendly match provided Brazil with an opportunity to rebound internationally and allowed key attacking players to regain scoring momentum. The comprehensive margin underscores the team's offensive depth during their international fixture.

stories.title: Iranian Foreign Minister Meets Army Chief Munir to Discuss Security Challenges
stories.summary:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi met with Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir in Rawalpindi on Monday to confer on regional security and collaborative approaches to shared security issues. According to the Inter-Services Public Relations, the high-level delegation's visit included discussions on mutual interests, geopolitical shifts, and regional stability.

During the meeting, Field Marshal Munir underlined the necessity of continuous engagement, strong mutual trust, and close coordination between Pakistan and Iran to foster regional peace. In response, Araghchi acknowledged Pakistan's contributions to regional stability and conveyed Tehran's commitment to deepening bilateral ties.

The Iranian foreign minister traveled to Pakistan to participate in the 30th Economic Cooperation Organization Council of Foreign Ministers meeting in Islamabad. Addressing the forum earlier, Araghchi emphasized Iran's pursuit of friendly neighborhood relations and cautioned that regional states must not permit their territories, airspace, or facilities to be utilized for launching attacks against other nations.

stories.title: New Zealand All-Rounder Mitchell Santner Ruled Out of India Test Series
stories.summary:
New Zealand all-rounder and limited-overs captain Mitchell Santner has been sidelined from the upcoming two-Test series against India due to a fractured bone in his hand. The injury places uncertainty on his availability for the subsequent four-Test series scheduled in Australia. The incident occurred during the fifth one-day international against India on Sunday when Santner was struck while batting, with subsequent scans confirming a fracture in his non-bowling right hand.

The two-Test series between New Zealand and India is set to begin on Thursday in Wellington and will conclude with a match in Christchurch starting November 27. New Zealand Cricket stated that Santner's return-to-play timeline is currently being evaluated, and updates regarding his participation in the Australia series, which begins in Perth on December 9, will be provided in due course.

To fill the vacancy in the 14-man squad, spin-bowling all-rounder Dean Foxcroft has been named as Santner's replacement. Foxcroft previously made his Test debut against Ireland in May. Because New Zealand's pitches typically favor seam bowling rather than spin, captain Tom Latham may depend on part-time spinners Glenn Phillips and Rachin Ravindra to support a four-man pace attack.

This upcoming red-ball series marks the first meeting between the two nations in the format since New Zealand achieved a historic 3-0 Test series victory in India in 2024. The loss of Santner is a notable blow to the team's depth as they prepare to face India on home soil before heading to Australia.

stories.title: Baidu Chief Warns of AI Bubble as Global Tech Leaders Gather for APEC
stories.summary:
Artificial intelligence integration is failing to generate higher profits for the majority of companies, according to Robin Li, the chief executive of Chinese technology giant Baidu. Speaking during a panel discussion in Shenzhen alongside business leaders ahead of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation meeting, Li described the current global technology environment as urgent, noting that the expansion of AI into application layers has fallen short of expectations.

Li pointed out that while foundational competition is intense, most firms are not seeing increased revenues or higher profits following AI adoption, warning that concerns over an AI bubble could materialize if the issue remains unaddressed. These remarks coincide with quarterly financial results from US chip titan Nvidia, its first since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO amid an affair scandal. That scandal has heightened scrutiny regarding how Chinese companies acquire powerful Nvidia chips despite US export controls.

Baidu itself has faced mounting financial challenges amid a prolonged domestic consumer slump that has impacted advertising cash flows. On Monday, the Beijing-based search engine provider reported its sixth consecutive drop in quarterly revenue, with Li acknowledging ongoing hurdles in online marketing. Market anxieties have also been amplified by warnings from international financial figures, such as IMF chief Kristalina Georgieva, who noted in October that a loss of investor confidence in AI returns could trigger global financial stability risks.

The discussions at APEC precede a scheduled meeting between Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, where both leaders are expected to address AI-related risks. Despite fierce technological rivalry between the two superpowers, growing calls emphasize the need for cooperation to manage the uncertainties surrounding the booming artificial intelligence sector.

stories.title: Shahid Khaqan Abbasi Criticizes Political System and Nawaz Sharif's Past Choices
stories.summary:
Former prime minister Shahid Khaqan Abbasi asserted that the failure to honor the public mandate is the fundamental driver of the ongoing political crisis in Pakistan. In an exclusive interview, Abbasi stated that the political trajectory could have been significantly different if Nawaz Sharif had acknowledged defeat following the general elections held on February 8, 2024. He argued that accepting the electoral outcome would have elevated Nawaz Sharif's political standing and helped his party rebuild public support.

Abbasi revealed that he had consistently urged Nawaz Sharif to prioritize the slogan of respecting the vote rather than pursuing power directly, though Nawaz typically responded with silence. Describing the current administration as operating on a temporary, daily-wage basis, Abbasi remarked that the government neither attained power through popular mandate nor will it depart through public choice, noting it will exit whenever it receives directives to do so. While stating he is unsatisfied with the government's overall performance, he acknowledged they are effective at maintaining their positions.

Commenting on the country's hybrid political framework, Abbasi noted he could not disagree with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi's assessment that the current system is malfunctioning. He also condemned authorities over the reported failure to transfer PTI founder Imran Khan to a hospital, characterizing the decision as a petty action and questioning the utility of ignoring court orders, while noting that Imran Khan had engaged in similar behavior previously.

Abbasi concluded that individuals and leaders who fail to learn valuable lessons from past mistakes will eventually be forced out of power. His remarks shed light on deep-seated governance concerns, the role of political mandates, and ongoing tensions within Pakistan's complex political landscape.

stories.title: کراچی کے علاقے بلدیہ رشید آباد میں فیکٹری میں آتشزدگی سے ڈیزل کا ٹینکر جل گیا
stories.summary:
کراچی کے علاقے بلدیہ رشید آباد میں ایک فیکٹری میں اچانک آگ بھڑک اٹھی جس پر قابو پانے کے لیے آٹھ فائر ٹینڈر اور اسنارکل مصروف عمل ہیں۔ فیکٹری کے اندر کپڑا، شیشہ اور دیگر مختلف سامان موجود تھا جو جل کر خاکستر ہو گیا۔

حادثے کے دوران فیکٹری میں کھڑا ایک ڈیزل کا ٹینکر بھی آگ کی لپیٹ میں آ کر جل گیا، جس کے نتیجے میں ڈیزل فضا اور سڑک پر پھیل گیا۔ اس خطرناک صورتحال کے پیش نظر فائر بریگیڈ کے عملے نے احتیاطی تدابیر اختیار کرتے ہوئے آس پاس کی دیگر فیکٹریوں کو بھی فوری طور پر خالی کروا لیا ہے۔

حادثے کے حوالے سے مزید نقصانات یا جانی نقصان کی کوئی تفصیلات تحال سامنے نہیں آئیں، تاہم امدادی کارروائیاں جاری ہیں۔ فائر فائٹرز آگ پر قابو پانے کے لیے اپنی تمام تر صلاحیتیں بروئے کار لارہے ہیں تاکہ مزید پھیلاؤ کو روکا جا سکے۔

stories.title: محکمہ موسمیات نے کراچی میں درجہ حرارت بڑھنے کی وجوہات واضح کر دیں
stories.summary:
محکمہ موسمیات نے شہر قائد کراچی میں بڑھتے ہوئے درجہ حرارت کی وجوہات بیان کرتے ہوئے بتایا ہے کہ خلیج بنگال میں سمندری طوفان کی تشکیل کے باعث خنک ہواؤں کی شدت میں کمی واقع ہوئی ہے۔ توقع کی جا رہی تھی کہ دن اور رات کے درجہ حرارت میں نمایاں کمی آئے گی مگر ایسا نہیں ہوا۔

محکمہ موسمیات کے مطابق آئندہ چوبیس گھنٹوں کے دوران شہر کا موسم خشک رہنے کا امکان ہے جبکہ رات کے وقت خنکی برقرار رہے گی۔ مزید برآں، سمندری طوفان 'اکوان' سے پاکستان کے کسی بھی ساحلی علاقے کو کوئی خطرہ نہیں ہے اور یہ طوفان بیس نومبر کو بھارتی ساحلی علاقوں سے ٹکرا سکتا ہے۔

محکمہ موسمیات کی پیشگوئی کے مطابق آنے والے چند روز تک کراچی میں دن کا درجہ حرارت بتیس سے چونتیس ڈگری سینٹی گریڈ کے درمیان جبکہ رات کا درجہ حرارت بیس سے بائیس ڈگری سینٹی گریڈ تک رہنے کی توقع ہے۔

stories.title: پاکستان اور ترکمانستان کا تجارت، توانائی اور دوطرفہ تعلقات بڑھانے پر اتفاق
stories.summary:
نائب وزیر اعظم و وزیر خارجہ اسحاق ڈار نے کہا ہے کہ پائیدار امن اور استحکام کے حصول کے لیے مذاکرات اور سفارت کاری ہی واحد مؤثر راستہ ہیں۔ انہوں نے ان خیالات کا اظہار ترکمانستان کے وزیر خارجہ راشد میردوف کے ہمراہ ایک مشترکہ پریس کانفرنس سے خطاب کرتے ہوئے کیا۔

اسحاق ڈار کا کہنا تھا کہ پاکستان اور ترکمانستان کے درمیان تجارت اور سرمایہ کاری کے شعبوں میں ترقی کے وسیع مواقع موجود ہیں۔ اس کے علاوہ توانائی، نقل و حمل اور عوامی روابط کے شعبوں میں بھی باہمی تعاون کو مزید وسعت دی جا سکتی ہے، اور مشترکہ بین الحکومتی کمیشن اس دوستی کو مضبوط معاشی شراکت داری میں بدلنے کا بنیادی فورم ہے۔

ترکمانستان کے وزیر خارجہ راشد میردوف نے علاقائی امن کے لیے پاکستان کے کردار اور سفارتی کاوشوں کو سراہا۔ انہوں نے شاندار مہمان نوازی پر پاکستانی قیادت کا شکریہ ادا کیا اور پاکستان کے ساتھ دوطرفہ تعلقات کو مزید فروغ دینے کے لیے اپنے غیر متزلزل عزم کا اعادہ کیا۔

stories.title: Pakistan Demands Halt to Israeli Attacks on Syria at UN
stories.summary:
During a United Nations Security Council briefing on the political and humanitarian situation in Syria, Pakistan strongly condemned ongoing Israeli military attacks and incursions into Syrian territory. Ambassador Syed Haider Shah, Pakistan’s Permanent Representative to the UN, urged an immediate halt to these violations and called for a complete withdrawal from occupied areas. Islamabad emphasized the importance of full compliance with the 1974 Disengagement Agreement and relevant Security Council resolutions, reaffirming that the occupied Syrian Golan remains Syrian territory under international law.

Ambassador Shah expressed support for the Syrian government's efforts to rebuild national institutions, advance political transitions, and foster stability. He noted that consolidating this progress requires a secure environment, economic opportunities, and sustained political engagement. Furthermore, Pakistan welcomed recent decisions by the United States, the European Union, and the United Kingdom to ease or lift economic sanctions on Syria, which have opened pathways for recovery, investment, and reconstruction. Shah stressed the necessity of turning these opportunities into tangible improvements for Syrian citizens through predictable humanitarian assistance.

On security and governance matters, Pakistan backed the integration of security and administrative structures in northeast Syria under a January 29 agreement, and praised a roadmap agreed upon by Syria, Jordan, and the United States for Suwaidah. Acknowledging the ongoing threat posed by Daesh and other militant networks, Shah called for coordinated international counter-terrorism cooperation. He also highlighted a joint statement and security committee agreement between Syria and Jordan from October 28 as positive steps for regional stability.

Concluding his remarks, Shah underscored that Syria's long-term recovery depends on respectful, practical international support while strictly safeguarding the nation's unity, sovereignty, and territorial integrity. He reiterated Pakistan's enduring solidarity with the Syrian population as they navigate reconstruction and political reform.

stories.title: Star Entertainment Appoints John Salomone as New Chief Financial Officer
stories.summary:
Australian casino operator Star Entertainment announced on Tuesday that Deputy Chief Financial Officer John Salomone will step into the role of group CFO, replacing Charlie Diao. Diao, who joined the firm earlier this year from its largest shareholder, US-based Bally’s Corporation, is transitioning to become the company's group chief risk officer to focus entirely on risk management functions.

The leadership shift comes amid a period of intense financial and regulatory scrutiny for Star Entertainment. In June, the New South Wales gaming regulator penalized the casino operator with a A$10 million ($6.75 million) fine for systemic failures linked to historical financial crime risks. Additionally, the Star Sydney casino was ordered to invest A$5 million to upgrade its technology and systems used to prevent and detect financial crimes.

John Salomone brings prior industry experience to his new position, having joined Star in 2024 and served as deputy CFO since June of the previous year. Before his tenure at Star Entertainment, Salomone worked as the finance chief for Crown Resorts. His appointment coincides with broader corporate stabilization efforts following various regulatory and financial setbacks since 2024.

Despite securing new investments and successfully refinancing its debt to avoid voluntary administration, Star Entertainment continues to navigate a challenging market environment. Following the announcement, the company's shares experienced a brief drop of up to 3% before stabilizing to trade flat at A$0.17 per share.

stories.title: Pakistan Cricket Board Appoints Shane Deitz as Women's Team Coach
stories.summary:
The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) named Australian Shane Deitz as the new head coach of the national women's cricket team on Tuesday. The 51-year-old is set to take charge ahead of an upcoming bilateral series against the West Indies, joining the squad directly in the Caribbean for his inaugural assignment. Deitz succeeds Wahab Riaz, who previously served as both mentor and head coach following the departure of Mohammad Wasim after the ICC Women's World Cup last year.

Deitz becomes only the third foreign coach in the history of the Pakistan women's team, following New Zealand's Mark Coles and Bermuda's David Hemp. Reflecting on his appointment, Deitz expressed deep honor and recalled cheering for Pakistan during their 1992 World Cup victory against England as a youngster. Looking forward, he outlined a long-term goal of preparing the team to deliver strong performances when Pakistan hosts the T20 World Cup in 2028, while acknowledging the substantial work required to reach world-class standards.

A former left-handed top-order batter and occasional wicketkeeper from Bankstown, New South Wales, Deitz played 66 first-class matches for South Australia before transitioning into a coaching career. His extensive resume includes coaching roles with Cricket Wellington in New Zealand, Bangladesh's women's team, Vanuatu Cricket, and the Netherlands women's team, where he helped secure ODI status. Most recently, he served as head coach of the West Indies women's team from July 2023 until October 2026, guiding them to consecutive T20 World Cup semi-finals.

Deitz's arrival marks the continuation of frequent coaching changes for the Pakistan women's squad, making him the sixth person to lead the team over the past three and a half years. The coaching position has seen various local and foreign appointments, interim arrangements, and fluctuating team results across international tournaments. Currently, the Pakistan team is participating in the ICC Emerging Nations Trophy in the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Australian Shares Reach One-Week Low Due to Mining and Financial Drops
stories.summary:
Australian shares declined during early trading on Tuesday, sliding for a fourth consecutive session and hitting a more than one-week low. The benchmark S&P/ASX 200 index dropped 1% to 8,956 points by 2315 GMT. The downward movement was primarily driven by heavy losses in the mining and financial sectors, compounded by weak commodity prices and cautionary remarks from the central bank regarding ongoing inflation risks.

Miners experienced a significant downturn, shedding 2.6% as iron ore and copper prices touched multi-month lows. This slump was influenced by sluggish Chinese economic data and concerns surrounding artificial intelligence spending, with major industry players BHP and Rio Tinto both recording declines of over 2%. Financial stocks also fell nearly 1%, pushed down by a 2% drop in National Australia Bank shares. These market pressures aligned with comments from Reserve Bank of Australia Governor Michele Bullock, who stated during a Sydney panel discussion that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.

The central bank recently raised its cash rate to an 18-year high of 4.85%, though it hinted that its current cycle of rate hikes may be nearing an end. Market participants are currently anticipating a rate hold during the RBA's upcoming meeting in early December. Meanwhile, energy stocks fell 1.3% as crude prices decreased due to expectations of a global supply surplus and improving oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz, affecting companies like Woodside Energy and Santos. Gold stocks similarly dropped 1.7% as bullion hit a one-year low amid a stronger U.S. dollar and expectations of a Federal Reserve rate hike next month.

In neighboring New Zealand, the benchmark S&P/NZX 50 index declined 0.4% to 14,251.99 points. The Reserve Bank of New Zealand warned that increasing global financial stability risks could pose significant shocks to the country, though it affirmed that the local financial system maintains its resilience.

stories.title: South Korean Shares Fall for Fourth Straight Day Amid US Tech Slump
stories.summary:
South Korean financial markets experienced a downturn on Tuesday, with shares declining for a fourth consecutive session. The benchmark KOSPI index dropped 74.24 points, or 1.46 percent, to settle at 5,026.26 by 0149 GMT, after having fallen by more than two percent earlier in the day. This downward trend was primarily driven by losses among chipmakers and technology stocks, reflecting broader concerns regarding the global artificial intelligence investment boom and a recent selloff in US markets.

The decline in US equities was partly fueled by fallout from Jensen Huang’s resignation as Nvidia CEO, which dampened enthusiasm for artificial intelligence stocks. Analysts, including Kiwoom Securities analyst Han Ji-young, noted that the psychological 5,000 mark for the index faces threats from slower anticipated artificial intelligence demand, though a recovery during sessions was expected after pricing in prior concerns.

Individual major equities saw notable reductions. Prominent chipmaker Samsung Electronics decreased by 2.41 percent, while industry peer SK Hynix fell 0.63 percent. Other heavyweights also suffered, with battery producer LG Energy Solution dropping 0.63 percent, Hyundai Motor slipping 1.88 percent, and its sister automaker Kia Corporation declining 2.84 percent. Additionally, POSCO Holdings lost 0.93 percent and Samsung BioLogics fell 0.21 percent.

Market breadth tilted heavily toward losers as 646 issues declined while only 229 advanced out of 909 total traded entities. Foreign investors acted as net sellers, offloading shares valued at 514.1 billion won, which equates to $384.88 million. Concurrently, the South Korean won weakened by 0.39 percent against the US dollar to 1,341.8 on the onshore settlement platform, compared to its previous close of 1,336.5. In fixed income markets, December futures on three-year treasury bonds dropped 0.06 points to 103.42, with the benchmark three-year bond yield rising by 1.9 basis points to 3.758 percent and the 10-year yield increasing by 1.6 basis points to 3.998 percent.

stories.title: Japan's Nikkei Average Slips More Than One Percent Amid Investor Caution
stories.summary:
Japan’s Nikkei share average experienced a notable decline on Tuesday, dropping more than one percent. The Nikkei 225 Index fell 1.1 percent to reach 58,998.39 by 0149 GMT. This downward movement in Tokyo tracked a broader selloff on Wall Street as market participants adopted a cautious stance, staying on the sidelines ahead of upcoming major events including Nvidia’s third-quarter earnings report and Anthropic’s initial public offering.

Artificial intelligence and semiconductor-related equities spearheaded the losses in Japan. Advantest dropped 5.07 percent, Kioxia Holdings retreated by 4.58 percent, and SoftBank Group lost 4.1 percent. Monex Securities analyst Yoshitaka Araya explained that caution surrounding Nvidia’s earnings and Anthropic’s debut discouraged aggressive buying, placing sustained pressure on stock valuations. Furthermore, sentiment cooled following United States government initiatives to further restrict China’s acquisition of advanced artificial intelligence chips from providers like Nvidia, ahead of a high-stakes encounter between US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping.

Other sectors in Tokyo also suffered contractions. Energy exploration equities fell 3.7 percent as oil prices decreased amid projections of a global supply surplus. Meanwhile, banking shares retreated by 3.07 percent due to declining US Treasury yields. Overall market breadth remained negative on the Nikkei 225, recording 62 advancers, 162 decliners, and one unchanged issue.

Among individual index movements, the steepest percentage losers were Ibiden down 5.44 percent, Furukawa Electric trading 5.35 percent lower, and Mitsui Kinzoku dropping 4.43 percent. Conversely, the top percentage gainers on the index were led by Recruit Holdings, which rose 3.72 percent, followed by Credit Saison up 2.59 percent, and Yokogawa Electric Corporation adding 2.32 percent.

stories.title: US Vice President Vance Asserts Trump Will Not Permit Forever War in Iran
stories.summary:
US Vice President JD Vance stated on Monday that President Donald Trump will prevent the ongoing military engagement with Iran from transforming into an extended commitment. Rejecting calls for a prolonged American presence, Vance emphasized during an interview with Fox News that the administration remains steadfast in its resolve to avoid another prolonged conflict. He asserted that regardless of external pressures demanding an indefinite military posture, the president is committed to concluding the conflict rather than sustaining a long-term deployment.

Vance addressed ongoing debates regarding the costs and duration of the conflict, explicitly stating that the administration will not tolerate a commitment lasting ten, fifteen, or even two years. He attributed calls for a permanent footprint to neoconservatives and foreign policy advocates, reiterating that the administration made a clear promise to voters to steer clear of overseas entanglements. Vance expressed absolute confidence that Trump will ultimately bring the conflict to a close with favorable outcomes for the American populace, noting there is no disagreement between him and the president regarding this strategic direction.

Addressing the political landscape, Vance acknowledged that the conflict has carried political repercussions for Republicans, particularly through elevated gasoline and energy prices that contributed to difficulties following the 2026 midterm elections. He remarked that President Trump has likewise acknowledged these political costs. Vance also pushed back against personal criticism regarding a memorandum of understanding related to Iran, suggesting that detractors utilized him as a surrogate target to attack the president directly, adding that he is content to serve as a protective shield for the head of state.

The remarks arrive amid intensified scrutiny over the administration's foreign policy choices and domestic political fallout. While critics continue to debate the long-term implications of the US posture toward Iran, Vance maintained that the leadership team speaks with a unified voice. The administration's stated objective remains focused on achieving a definitive resolution without falling into the trap of an open-ended foreign military campaign.

stories.title: Thai Baht Holds Steady Against US Dollar During Tuesday Trading Session
stories.summary:
The Thai baht maintained a steady position against the US dollar on Tuesday, recording a slight increase after trading within a narrow bandwidth. According to data provided by LSEG, the local currency showed resilience during the early morning hours.

At 0220 GMT, the Thai baht traded 0.07 percent higher, standing at 33.84 against the greenback. Throughout the session, the currency moved within a constrained range spanning from 33.845 to 33.898 per dollar.

This performance follows the previous session's close, where the currency finished at 33.865 per dollar. The minimal movement highlights a period of relative calm for the baht in foreign exchange markets.

stories.title: NDMA Issues Severe Drought High Alert for Parts of Sindh
stories.summary:
The National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), through its National Emergency Operations Centre, has issued a high alert for severe drought conditions across specific parts of Sindh and Balochistan. The affected regions include Umerkot, Tharparkar, Mirpurkhas, and Sujawal districts in Sindh, alongside Chagai and Washuk districts in Balochistan. This escalating crisis is primarily driven by below-normal rainfall, prolonged dry weather, rising temperatures, and altered monsoon patterns.

Temperatures in the impacted Sindh districts are currently hovering one to three degrees Celsius above normal levels. This persistent water shortage is severely damaging agriculture and crop production, leading to heightened food security concerns. In response, the Sindh government has recently decided to launch a detailed survey covering Tharparkar and Umarkot to assess critical issues such as clean water access, education, food shortages, livestock conditions, and mother and child health.

Authorities have specifically directed relief efforts toward the Diplo, Dahli, Chachro, and Nagar Parkar regions, with a strong emphasis on prioritizing women and children. Officials are actively considering various intervention mechanisms, including food provisions, cash financial assistance, food vouchers, and the Benazir Income Support Program. Earlier, Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah resolved to declare Tharparkar a calamity-hit district while ordering immediate operational steps to tackle the drought.

This high-level intervention matters significantly for local communities whose livelihoods and daily survival are directly threatened by agricultural collapse and water scarcity. By deploying targeted welfare programs and comprehensive local surveys, the government aims to mitigate the immediate humanitarian fallout of the prolonged dry weather and secure basic supplies for vulnerable populations.

stories.title: Pakistani and Iranian Officials Discuss Regional Security and Cooperation
stories.summary:
A high-level Iranian delegation, spearheaded by Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, met with Field Marshal Syed Asim Munir, Chief of Army Staff and Chief of Defence Forces, in Rawalpindi on November 16. The high-level discussions, detailed by the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR), centered on mutual interests, evolving geopolitical developments, and regional security dynamics. Both sides thoroughly explored potential avenues for jointly addressing common security challenges.

During the meeting, Field Marshal Asim Munir emphasized the vital necessity of sustained engagement, mutual trust, and close coordination between the two neighboring countries to foster regional peace and stability. In response, Foreign Minister Araghchi acknowledged Pakistan's constructive role in promoting regional stability and articulated his nation's firm desire to further strengthen bilateral relations.

In a parallel development concerning broader Middle Eastern tensions, US Vice President JD Vance stated on Monday that President Donald Trump will prevent the ongoing conflict with Iran from escalating into an extended military commitment. Speaking in an interview with Fox News, Vance dismissed calls for a prolonged US military footprint and reaffirmed the administration's dedication to avoiding another protracted war.

Vance noted that there is complete alignment between him and President Trump regarding the conflict's trajectory, emphasizing that the administration intends to bring the engagement to a close rather than sustain a long-term presence. These remarks arrive amid an ongoing debate in Washington regarding the exact scope and duration of American military involvement tied to the Iranian conflict.
